entries.lemma: single-site lexical decisions of Isaiah 11
entries.literal: his smelling; and the fatling together; light-hole(?); stretched out(?); his resting place, glory; his hand, to acquire; the coastlands of the sea; the harassers of Judah; on the shoulder; the stretching-out of their hand; with the heat(?) of his wind; in sandals; counsel and might
entries.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; alternatives from JPS 1917 and NJPS recorded in commentary
entries.wohChoice: 11:2 MT's six qualities in three pairs, ʿēṣāh 'counsel', gᵉḇûrāh 'might' (ASV; LXX 'piety' and the seven-gifts tradition in commentary). 11:3 'his delight shall be in the fear of YHWH' (ASV, JPS 1917; literal 'his smelling' and NJPS 'he shall sense the truth' in commentary). 11:6 the Masoretic verbless clause 'and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together' (1QIsaᵃ/LXX 'shall feed' in commentary); gār 'dwell'. 11:8 'the hole of the asp … the adder's den … put his hand' (ASV). 11:10 mᵉnuḥāṯô kāḇôḏ 'his resting place shall be glory' (predicate noun kept, kāḇôḏ = 'glory'). 11:11 supplied 'set' (ASV), liqnôṯ 'to recover', ʾiyyê hayyām 'the coastlands of the sea' (as 24:15). 11:13 'those who harass Judah' (ASV construal), 'harass' for both ṣrr forms. 11:14 'swoop down upon the shoulder of the Philistines', ASV verbal rendering of the closing nominal clauses. 11:15 baʿyām rûḥô 'with his scorching wind' (ASV), 'cause men to march over dryshod' (ASV, 'men' supplied).
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Hebrew is rare, elliptical or ambiguous, and the line keeps a standard rendering (ASV, usually shared by JPS 1917) while the commentary reports the alternatives, and three items depart from ASV wording. (a) 11:10: ASV and JPS 1917 turn the predicate noun kāḇôḏ into the adjective 'glorious' and NJPS has 'honored'; the line keeps the noun, 'his resting place shall be glory', because wave ruling 6 makes 'glory' for kāḇôḏ strict, the book renders other verbless kāḇôḏ clauses literally (6:3; 24:23), and a predicate noun of quality is ordinary Hebrew syntax. (b) 11:11: ʾiyyê hayyām is 'the coastlands of the sea', not ASV and JPS 1917 'the islands of the sea', for concordance with the stable 24:15 ('in the coastlands of the sea') and 42:4 ('the coastlands'); ʾî denotes coast and island alike (BDB), and the places meant are the Mediterranean shores and islands, which 'coastlands' covers. (c) 11:14: ʿwp is 'swoop down' for ASV and JPS 1917 'fly down'; the verb is 'to fly', and in context it is the descent of a bird of prey on its victim (NJPS 'pounce'), which 'swoop down' states without adding anything to the verb's sense. At 11:3 the Hiphil of rwḥ is 'smell, take in the scent' (Lev 26:31; Amos 5:21), and NJPS notes that the meaning is uncertain; the idiomatic 'delight' is the reading of ASV and JPS 1917 and is kept, with NJPS's 'sense the truth' and the proposed deletion as a dittography reported. At 11:6 MT has no verb for the third pair; NJPS records that 1QIsaᵃ and the LXX read 'shall feed', and the line keeps MT under mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah. At 11:8 mᵉʾûraṯ and hāḏāh occur only here (NJPS: 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'), so ASV's contextual 'den' and 'put' are kept. At 11:11 MT has no verb governing yāḏô; ASV's supplied 'set' is kept, and ʾiyyê hayyām follows the stable 24:15 'the coastlands of the sea' rather than ASV 'islands'. At 11:13 ṣōrᵉrê yᵉhûḏāh may be objective (Judah's enemies; ASV, JPS 1917) or subjective (NJPS 'Judah's harassment'); the ASV construal is kept and the subjective reading, which fits the verse's second half, is reported. At 11:14 kāṯēp̄ may be the topographic 'slope' (Josh 15:8-11; NJPS 'the back of Philistia'), and the closing clauses are nominal in Hebrew; ASV's rendering is kept. At 11:15 baʿyām is a hapax (NJPS 'might', 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'), and ASV 'scorching' is kept; wᵉhiḏrîḵ ban-nᵉʿālîm is literally 'make (them) tread in sandals', and ASV's supplied object 'men' is kept and identified as supplied in commentary. Wave I-4 extension, limited to the ʾî item: the singular hāʾî hazzeh at 20:6 is 'this coastland', concordant with 'the coastlands of the sea' at 11:11 and the stable 24:15 and 42:4 (ASV and JPS 1917 'coast-land', NJPS 'coastland', checked). Here it is the Philistine coast of Ashdod (20:1). Wave I-4 extension, limited to the ʾî item: yōšᵉḇê ʾî at 23:2 and 23:6 is 'inhabitants of the coastland', concordant with 11:11, 24:15, 40:15 and 20:6 (ASV 'the coast', JPS 1917 'coast-land', NJPS 'coastland dwellers', checked on Sefaria and bible-api.com). Here it is the Phoenician coast together with island Tyre.

entries.strongs: H1348 (gēʾûṯ); cf. H1347 (gāʾôn), H1342 (gāʾāh). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: gēʾûṯ 'a rising up; majesty; pride', noun of the root gʾh 'rise, be high'
entries.literal: a rising, loftiness
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'he hath done excellent things' (12:5); JPS 1917 and NJPS 'gloriously' (12:5); 'majesty' (Ps 93:1); 'pride' (Isa 28:1, 3)
entries.wohChoice: 'majesty / majestic' where gēʾûṯ is the majesty of YHWH or of his acts: 12:5 'he has done majestic things'; 26:10 'the majesty of YHWH' (stable, already so printed). Context clauses: 'pride' where gēʾûṯ is human arrogance (Isa 28:1, 3 'the crown of pride', when drafted); the physical sense 'rising, column' where it is the upward movement of smoke or sea (Isa 9:17 Heb. gēʾûṯ ʿāšān 'a column of smoke', as the chapter 9 draft prints it; cf. Ps 89:10). Never 'glory' or 'gloriously', which are reserved for kāḇôḏ.
entries.rationale: Gēʾûṯ belongs to the root gʾh 'rise, be high', the root of gāʾôn, which the book renders 'majesty' (24:14; 2:10, 19, 21 under hadar-splendor-isaiah). The lexica give it a physical sense 'rising' and the evaluative senses 'majesty' and 'pride' (BDB; HALOT). Of YHWH it is the majesty he wears (Ps 93:1), and the stable chapter 26:10 already prints 'the majesty of YHWH', so 'majestic' at 12:5 keeps the root concordant within the book. The usual renderings of 12:5 are ASV 'excellent things', in an older sense of 'excellent' ('surpassing') that modern English has lost, and JPS 1917 / NJPS 'gloriously' (both checked on Sefaria). 'Gloriously' would put on a gʾh-noun the English that wave rule 6 reserves strictly for kāḇôḏ. The clause also echoes gāʾōh gāʾāh, the cognate verb that opens the Song of the Sea (Exod 15:1, 21), the song quoted at Isa 12:2. 'Majesty' is a standard lexical gloss and carries no interpretive load, so the claim is direct. The pejorative and physical senses are recorded as context clauses so that one entry governs the lemma book-wide. Wave I-5: the context clause for human arrogance is applied as forecast: 28:1, 3 ʿăṭereṯ gēʾûṯ 'the crown of pride' (ASV, JPS 1917, Koren; NJPS 'the proud crowns').

entries.lemma: single-site lexical and syntactic decisions of Isaiah 12
entries.partOfSpeech: mixed (verb forms, nominal clause, nouns, participles)
entries.literal: let your anger turn and you comfort me; God (is) my salvation / the God of my salvation; springs of the salvation; call on his name; cause to remember; made known; she who dwells (in) Zion
entries.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; JPS 1917 'proclaim his name', 'This is made known'; NJPS 'Your wrath has turned back', 'the God who gives me triumph', 'fountains of triumph', 'proclaim', 'declare', 'You who dwell in Zion'; NRSV 'royal Zion' (recalled, not verified)
entries.wohChoice: 12:1 a statement, 'your anger has turned away, and you comfort me' (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS), against the strict jussive wish; the verb 'turn away' as in the refrain bekhol-zot-lo-shav-appo-refrain-isaiah, whose reversal the clause is. 12:2 nominal clause 'Behold, God is my salvation' (ASV, JPS 1917), with the NJPS construct noted. 12:3 'the wells of salvation' (ASV, JPS 1917), with the lexical sense 'springs / fountains' in commentary. 12:4 'call on his name' (central qara-b-shem-yhwh), 'make known his deeds among the peoples' (as in ASV Ps 105:1), 'make mention' (ASV, JPS 1917). 12:5 qere participle as a wish, 'let this be known' (ASV, NJPS). 12:6 'O inhabitant of Zion' (ASV collective). Quotation marks: the first song runs 12:1b-2 and the second 12:4b-6, with 12:3 as narration between them (JPS 1917 and NJPS mark the same extents).
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator flagged a choice among standard renderings. The Editor keeps the Masoretic text and the ASV baseline unless the corpus's concordance rules require a change, and records the alternatives. (1) The short form yāšōḇ and the non-consecutive ûṯᵉnaḥămēnî, if pressed, give a wish. ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS read a statement, which suits a thanksgiving (ʾôḏᵉḵā), and the Vulgate also has a past statement (recalled; the LXX was not verified). The Translator's report that the versions read a wish is therefore not followed. (2) ʾēl has the same form in the absolute and the construct. The nominal clause (ASV, JPS 1917) is kept, and NJPS's construct is noted. (3) maʿyān is a spring or fountain (BDB; HALOT), but 'wells' is the established English of the verse and matches šāʾaḇ 'draw water'. The central maʿyān entry (Gen 7:11 'fountains of the great deep') is cosmic in scope and is not extended. (4) 12:4a repeats Ps 105:1 = 1 Chr 16:8 word for word, and the line follows ASV's wording of the psalm. qārāʾ bᵉšēm is the invocation formula governed by central qara-b-shem-yhwh. The 'proclaim' sense (JPS 1917, NJPS; cf. Exod 34:5) is recorded. When psalms-woh 105 or a Chronicles translation is drafted, a central parallel entry on the model of isa-2-2-4-mic-4-1-3-zion-pilgrimage-parallel-cross-corpus is recommended. (5) mûḏaʿaṯ is a participle (the qere; the ketiv is the Pual form). It is read as a wish after the imperative, with ASV and NJPS, and JPS 1917's statement is noted. (6) yôšeḇeṯ + place name is the idiom for a town's population (Mic 1:11-13), so the ASV collective is kept, and the enthroned-city reading is noted. None of these choices carries a lens.

entries.strongs: H8141 (šānāh); H7916 (śāḵîr). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: śāḵîr 'hired worker, day-labourer' in the time-formula kišnê śāḵîr 'as the years of a hireling'
entries.partOfSpeech: prepositional phrase (kᵉ + construct plural noun + noun)
entries.literal: like the years of a hired one
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'as the years of a hireling' (16:14), 'according to the years of a hireling' (21:16); JPS 1917 'as the years of a hireling' (16:14); NJPS 'fixed like the years of a hired laborer' (16:14)
entries.wohChoice: 'as the years of a hireling' at every site of the formula: 16:14 'Within three years, as the years of a hireling'; 21:16 (forward scope within wave I-4, to be added by the chapter 21 Editor). ASV's 'according to' at 21:16 is not followed, so that the one Hebrew phrase has one English rendering in the book. 'Hireling' is a gender-neutral noun and stays (wave I-4 ruling 13 does not apply).
entries.rationale: The phrase kišnê śāḵîr occurs twice in Isaiah, at 16:14 (Moab's three years) and 21:16 (Kedar's one year), and wave I-4 ruling 14 fixes one rendering for both. The śāḵîr is a worker hired for a fixed term, whose time is counted exactly and not exceeded (Lev 25:50 kîmê śāḵîr; Job 7:1 kîmê śāḵîr yāmāyw 'his days are like the days of a hireling'), so the simile means that the term is exact and will not be extended (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27, ad loc.; NJPS supplies 'fixed' to make the point). 'As the years of a hireling' is the reading of ASV and JPS 1917 at 16:14 (checked: ASV in the data-library copy, JPS 1917 on Sefaria). ASV's 'according to' at 21:16 varies the English for no Hebrew reason, and is therefore not followed. The rendering is the standard one and carries no lens, so the claim is direct. Wave I-4 (ruling 14): kišnê śāḵîr at 21:16 is 'as the years of a hireling', the same wording as 16:14. ASV and JPS 1917 have 'according to the years of a hireling' and NJPS 'fixed like the years of a hired laborer'. MT bᵉʿôḏ šānāh 'Within a year' is kept against the reported 1QIsaᵃ 'three years'.

entries.strongs: H1347 (gāʾôn); H1341 (gēʾ); H1346 (gaʾăwāh); H5678 (ʿeḇrāh); H907 (bad 'idle talk'). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: nouns of the root gʾh 'rise, be high' used of human arrogance, with ʿeḇrāh 'overflowing, excess'
entries.literal: height / loftiness; lofty; haughtiness; overflowing (of anger or arrogance)
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'the pride of Moab … very proud … his arrogancy, and his pride, and his wrath; his boastings are nought'; JPS 1917 'his haughtiness, and his pride, and his arrogancy'; NJPS 'Moab's pride — Most haughty is he — Of his pride and haughtiness and arrogance, And of the iniquity in him'
entries.wohChoice: 16:6 (recorded departure from the wave I-4 ruling 2 default 'majesty', which stays in force for the majesty of YHWH and of things he gives: 24:14; 2:10, 19, 21 under hadar-splendor-isaiah): gāʾôn of Moab's arrogance is 'pride', gaʾăwāh 'haughtiness' (as stable 13:11), gēʾ 'proud': 'the pride of Moab, that he is very proud, of his haughtiness and his pride and his wrath; his boasts are nothing'. ʿeḇrāh keeps ASV 'wrath' (the 'insolence / arrogance' sense in commentary); lōʾ-ḵēn baddāyw keeps ASV's sense 'his boasts are nothing' (NJPS's prepositional reading in commentary). Further sites of gāʾôn as human arrogance take 'pride' only by their Editor's recorded decision (the chapter 23 Editor extends the entry to 23:9). Never 'glory', which is reserved for kāḇôḏ. Context clause for the planned concordance pass (stable lines, not reopened): gāʾôn of human arrogance is rendered otherwise at 13:11 'the arrogance of the proud' (gᵉʾôn zēḏîm) and 14:11 'Your pomp' (gᵉʾônᵉḵā); gāʾôn in the positive sense is 'pride' at 4:2 and 13:19; gaʾăwāh is 'pride' at 9:8 and 25:11.
entries.rationale: Isa 16:6 packs four words of the root gʾh into one line, gᵉʾôn-môʾāḇ gēʾ mᵉʾōḏ gaʾăwāṯô ûḡᵉʾônô, and each needs its own English so the reader can see the repetition. Ruling 2 makes 'majesty' the default for gāʾôn but allows a recorded departure where the idiom forbids it; 'the majesty of Moab' would turn an indictment into praise, so the departure 'pride' is taken, with ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (all checked) and with the stable 13:19 'the pride of the Chaldeans'. gaʾăwāh then takes 'haughtiness', which is how the stable 13:11 renders it ('the haughtiness of the ruthless'); the draft's 'arrogance' is not kept because 13:11 uses 'arrogance' for gāʾôn, and the swap would cross the two words between neighbouring chapters. The stable chapters are not fully concordant: 9:8 and 25:11 (also of Moab) render gaʾăwāh 'pride'. Those lines are not reopened here, and the inconsistency is reported for a later concordance pass. ʿeḇrāh is 'overflowing', used of fury and of arrogant excess (BDB; Prov 21:24 bᵉʿeḇraṯ zāḏôn); ASV's 'wrath' is kept, and NJPS's list ends in 'arrogance'. In lōʾ-ḵēn baddāyw the line takes bad as 'idle talk, boasting' (BDB bad III) with ASV, while NJPS reads the suffixed preposition bᵉḏê, 'And of the iniquity in him' (its note cites Nah 2:13; Hab 2:13; Job 39:25). The parallel Jer 48:29-30 has six terms (adding gobhô and rum libbô) and the same ʿeḇrāṯô wᵉlōʾ-ḵēn baddāyw (Hebrew checked on Sefaria). Post-review (wave I-4 Reviewer): the wohChoice is scoped to the recorded departures and does not state a book-wide rule, because the stable lines render gāʾôn of human arrogance as 'arrogance' (13:11) and 'pomp' (14:11); those sites are listed as a context clause for the planned concordance pass. The renderings are standard lexical glosses and carry no lens, so the claim is direct. Wave I-4 extension (Isa 23): gᵉʾôn kol-ṣᵉḇî at 23:9, the pride that YHWH profanes, is 'pride' (ASV and JPS 1917 'the pride of all glory'; NJPS folds the phrase into 'all glorious beauty', checked on Sefaria). The recorded departure from the default 'majesty' (hadar-splendor-isaiah) applies, as at 13:19 and 16:6.

entries.lemma: tense of the imperfects in the Moab lament, Isa 16:7, 9-11, aligned with the stable chapter 15
entries.literal: wails … you moan; I weep … I drench you; is not sung … is not shouted … does not tread; sound
entries.standardEnglish: ASV and JPS 1917 future ('shall Moab wail … shall ye mourn … I will weep … there shall be no singing'); NJPS jussive at 16:7 ('let Moab howl'), present at 16:9 ('I weep') and 16:10-11
entries.wohChoice: English present for the lament's imperfects at 16:7, 9, 10 and 11 ('Moab wails for Moab; everyone wails … you moan'; 'I weep … I drench you'; 'there is no singing … no treader treads'; 'my inner parts sound'), matching the stable chapter 15 (15:2 'Moab wails'; 15:3 'everyone wails'; 15:5 'My heart cries out'). Perfects keep their own English (16:8 'languish', 'have struck down'; 16:9 'has fallen'; 16:10 'I have made the shout cease'). The frame formulas keep the future: 16:12 wᵉhāyāh 'And it shall come to pass', 16:14 'shall be brought into contempt'. Does not govern the plea of 16:1-5.
entries.rationale: The Hebrew imperfect in poetry does not mark time by itself: it can express present, future or repeated action, and in a lament the present is the natural English (Joüon-Muraoka §113; Waltke-O'Connor §31). Isa 15 and 16:7-11 are one lament, and 16:7 repeats 15:3's kullōh yᵉyêlîl word for word, so wave I-4 ruling 3 requires the same English tense in both chapters; chapter 15 is stable and prints the present throughout. ASV and JPS 1917 read the imperfects as futures, taking the lament as prediction, and NJPS reads 16:7 as a jussive ('let Moab howl'), which the short form yᵉyêlîl permits but does not require (all three checked). The claim is inferred, not direct, because the choice among present, future and jussive is a reading of the verbal system in context, not something the forms decide. The rulings that bind the frame verses (16:12, 14) are left future, because there the weqatal and the dated prediction mark the future explicitly. This entry follows the method of poem-tense-outstretched-hand-isaiah-9: one tense policy for one poem, with its soft points disclosed in commentary (here 16:7, where NJPS's jussive is a real alternative).

entries.strongs: H4578 (mēʿeh, plural mēʿîm); H7130 (qereḇ); cf. H3820 (lēḇ). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: mēʿîm 'internal organs, innards' as the seat of feeling; qereḇ 'inward part, midst'
entries.literal: my innards … and my inward part
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'my heart … mine inward parts'; JPS 1917 'my heart … mine inward parts'; NJPS 'my heart … my very soul'; KJV 'my bowels … mine inward parts'
entries.wohChoice: mēʿîm as the seat of feeling is 'inner parts': 16:11 'my inner parts sound like a lyre for Moab'; with qereḇ beside it, qereḇ is 'inmost being' ('and my inmost being for Kir-heres'). 'Heart' is kept for lēḇ (stable 15:5 'My heart cries out for Moab'). Context clause: where mēʿîm is the body as the source of offspring the stable line has 'body' (48:19 'the offspring of your body') and is not reopened; future sites of the emotional sense (e.g. 63:15 hᵃmôn mēʿeyḵā) should take 'inner parts' unless their Editor records a departure.
entries.rationale: mēʿîm are the internal organs (BDB; HALOT), felt in Hebrew as the place where grief and longing stir (Jer 4:19 mēʿay mēʿay; Song 5:4; Isa 63:15). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS render the word 'my heart' at 16:11 (all checked), a fair idiomatic equivalent, but the stable 15:5, in the same lament over Moab, already gives 'heart' to lēḇ, and a reader of the English would take the two as one word. The book's practice is to keep distinct Hebrew nouns apart where English allows it (cf. hadar-splendor-isaiah, geut-majesty-isaiah), so 'inner parts' is chosen as a plain lexical gloss that avoids both 'heart' and the comic modern sense of KJV's 'bowels'. qirbî, ASV's 'inward parts', then needs a different English, and 'inmost being' gives the sense of qereḇ 'the inside' without importing 'soul' (NJPS), which in this corpus belongs to nep̄eš. The parallel Jer 48:36 has libbî 'my heart' twice where Isaiah has mēʿay … qirbî (Hebrew checked on Sefaria), which shows the words are interchangeable in the lament formula; the commentary reports it, and the Isaiah line still translates Isaiah's nouns. The choice is a standard gloss and carries no lens, so the claim is direct.

entries.lemma: the Moab lament shared by Isa 15-16 and Jer 48
entries.literal: (not applicable)
entries.standardEnglish: ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS translate each book on its own text; NJPS footnotes the Jeremiah readings at Isa 16:7 ('men') and 16:9 ('A ravager has come down')
entries.wohChoice: The Isaiah line translates Isaiah's Masoretic text and is not harmonized with Jeremiah; the Jeremiah differences are reported in commentary at each verse. Verse map with the differences that affect the English (Hebrew of Jer 48 checked on Sefaria): Isa 16:6 // Jer 48:29-30 (pride list; Jer adds gobhô, rum libbô, and has gēʾeh for gēʾ); 16:7 // Jer 48:31 (Jer is in the first person, ʾêlîl … ʾezʿāq 'I wail … I cry out', with 3ms yehgeh, against Isaiah's yᵉyêlîl 'Moab wails' and 2mp tehgû 'you moan'; Isa ʾăšîšê 'raisin-cakes' / Jer ʾanšê 'men'; Kir-hareseth / Kir-heres); 16:8-9 // Jer 48:32 (Jer mibbᵉḵî yaʿzēr ʾeḇkeh-lāḵ 'more than the weeping of Jazer I weep for you' against Isa ʾeḇkeh biḇḵî yaʿzēr 'I weep with the weeping of Jazer'; Isa hêḏāḏ / Jer šōḏēḏ 'destroyer'; Isa qᵉṣîrēḵ 'harvest' / Jer bᵉṣîrēḵ 'vintage'); 16:10 // Jer 48:33 (Jer adds ûmēʾereṣ môʾāḇ 'and from the land of Moab' and ends hêḏāḏ lōʾ hêḏāḏ 'the shout is no shout'); 16:11 // Jer 48:36 (Isa mēʿay … qirbî, kakkinnôr / Jer libbî twice, kaḥălilîm 'like flutes'; Isa lᵉqîr ḥāreś 'for Kir-heres' / Jer ʾel-ʾanšê qîr-ḥereś 'for the men of Kir-heres'); 16:12 // Jer 48:35 (the high place). Isa 15:4-6 // Jer 48:34 and 15:2-3 // Jer 48:37-38 complete the overlap.
entries.rationale: Isa 15:2-16:12 and Jer 48:29-38 share a lament over Moab, often word for word but in a different order, and wave I-4 ruling 3 requires the parallel to be flagged. The relation between the two (whether Jeremiah reuses Isaiah, or both draw on an older Moab oracle; cf. Isa 16:13 'the word that YHWH spoke concerning Moab in time past') is debated in the commentaries and is not decided here (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, ad loc.). The Isaiah line translates Isaiah's own text under mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah, because harmonizing with Jeremiah would make the base text eclectic. The verse map records the differences that affect the English (completed after the wave I-4 review, which found four omitted), so that a later jeremiah-woh Editor can match the shared wording or record a departure. The jeremiah-woh translation does not yet exist, so the entry stays in the overlay; when Jer 48 is drafted, the orchestrator should promote it to a central parallel entry on the model of isa-2-2-4-mic-4-1-3-zion-pilgrimage-parallel-cross-corpus. The record is a textual fact and carries no lens, so the claim is direct.

entries.lemma: single-site lexical and syntactic decisions of Isaiah 16
entries.literal: send a lamb of the ruler of the land from Sela toward the wilderness; like a wandering bird, a nest sent away; daughters of Moab; decision; the presser; the trampler are finished; quick of righteousness; the lords of nations struck its choice vines; the shout; he appears … he wearies; and it is made light, the weight/glory; the multitude the great
entries.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; JPS 1917 'the lambs', 'From the crags', 'execute justice', 'Whose choice plants did overcome The lords of nations', 'when it is seen that Moab hath wearied himself'; NJPS 'Dispatch as messenger the ruler of the land', 'Moab's villagers', 'Offer counsel', 'violence', 'zealous for equity', 'To Baale-goiim', 'when it has become apparent that Moab has gained nothing'
entries.wohChoice: 16:1 'Send the lamb for the ruler of the land, from Sela toward the wilderness' (kar singular; tribute reading as ASV; Sela a place name, as 42:11; directional -āh). 16:2 singular simile 'like a wandering bird, a scattered nest' and 'the daughters of Moab' (ASV, JPS 1917), ASV's supplied 'so' dropped. 16:3 pᵉlîlāh 'execute justice' (ASV, JPS 1917), with the note that it is not mišpāṭ. 16:4 hammēṣ 'the extortioner' (ASV); tammû rōmēs 'those who trample'. 16:5 mᵉhîr ṣeḏeq 'swift in righteousness' (ASV's supplied 'to do' dropped). 16:8 'the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches' (ASV). 16:9-10 hêḏāḏ 'the shout' at both sites, without ASV's supplied '[battle]' / '[vintage]'. 16:12 both verbs kept, 'when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself' (ASV, MT). 16:14 'the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt, with all the great multitude' (article, no suffix; ASV 'his').
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator flagged a choice among standard renderings, and the Editor keeps the Masoretic text and the ASV baseline unless the book's concordance rules or the Hebrew grammar require a change; the alternatives are recorded in commentary. (1) kar 'lamb' is singular and may be collective; the tribute reading fits Moab's lamb tribute under Mesha (2 Kgs 3:4), while NJPS's 'Dispatch as messenger' is marked uncertain in its own note. Sela keeps the place-name reading of the stable 42:11 and NJPS; JPS 1917's 'crags' is noted. (2) The simile is singular in Hebrew, and bᵉnôṯ môʾāḇ may mean the women or the dependent towns of Moab (cf. Num 21:25 'Heshbon and all its daughters'); NJPS's 'villagers' is recorded. (3) pᵉlîlāh is a rare noun for decision or arbitration (from pll); 'execute justice' is kept as the established English, and the commentary warns that 'justice' in 16:5 is mišpāṭ. (4) mēṣ occurs only here and is usually derived from mîṣ 'press' (Prov 30:33); 'extortioner' is ASV. (5) māhîr is 'quick' and also 'skilled' (Ps 45:2 Heb.; Ezra 7:6), so 'swift in righteousness' keeps the adjective without ASV's supplied verb. (6) At 16:8 the subject of hālᵉmû is ambiguous; ASV's reading is kept, and JPS 1917's (the vines overpower their drinkers) and NJPS's (a place name Baale-goiim, marked uncertain) are recorded. (7) hêḏāḏ is the treaders' shout and also a war cry (Jer 25:30; 51:14); one English word keeps the repetition visible. (8) The near-identical nirʾāh … nilʾāh at 16:12 are kept as MT; deletion as dittography is reported only. (9) At 16:14 the article in hehāmôn hārāḇ is translated as such. JPS 1917 and NJPS were checked on Sefaria and ASV in the data-library copy; NRSV and LXX readings are not used. None of these choices carries a lens.

entries.lemma: single-site lexical, syntactic and text-critical decisions of Isaiah 17
entries.partOfSpeech: mixed (nouns, construct chains, participles, a Pilpel verb, place names)
entries.literal: ruin(?), a fallen heap; the cities of Aroer; and the remnant of Aram, like the glory of; the glory of Jacob; harvest; the valley of Rephaim; in her branches, the fruitful one; the thicket and the treetop; the cities of his stronghold; plantings of pleasantness; a shoot of a stranger; you make grow(?); a heap of harvest; sick / inheritance; tumult … roar; wheel, whirl; storm-wind; he is not; our plunderers
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: 'a ruinous heap', 'The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down', 'and the remnant of Syria; they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel', 'the harvestman', 'in the outmost branches of a fruitful tree', 'the forsaken places in the wood and on the mountain top', 'pleasant plants … strange slips', 'thou hedgest it in … the harvest fleeth away in the day of grief', 'the whirling dust before the storm', 'them that rob us'. JPS 1917: 'make it to grow', 'A heap of boughs', 'plants of pleasantness … slips of a stranger'. NJPS: 'the mass of Israelites', 'tumbleweed before a gale', 'a delightful sapling … a disappointing slip', 'you see it grow … the branches wither away'. KJV: 'the harvest shall be a heap'. (ASV, KJV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 via Sefaria API v3; checked 2026-11-26.)
entries.wohChoice: 17:1 'a ruinous heap' (MT mᵉʿî as a by-form of ʿî; the lᵉʿî / dittography conjecture in commentary). 17:2 MT 'The cities of Aroer are forsaken' (the LXX-based emendation 'forsaken for ever' in commentary); wᵉrāḇᵉṣû rendered as a relative clause, 'which shall lie down' (ASV, JPS 1917), so that the masculine verb is referred to the flocks and not to the feminine cities (post-review refinement). 17:3 the accentual construal 'and the remnant of Aram; they shall be like the glory of the children of Israel' (ASV), with the JPS 1917 / NJPS subject reading in commentary. 17:3-4 kāḇôḏ 'glory' (strict wave concordance; NJPS 'mass' and the weight sense in commentary). 17:5 qāṣîr 'the harvester' (ASV 'harvestman', NJPS 'reaper'); ʿēmeq rᵉp̄āʾîm 'the valley of Rephaim', a place name, with the overlay rephaim-shades-dead-isaiah-26 and the central refaim-giant-peoples deliberately NOT applied. 17:6 'in the branches of the fruitful tree' (JPS 1917; ASV's added 'outmost' dropped). 17:9 MT 'the wood and the mountain top' (ASV), with the LXX 'Amorites and Hivites' in commentary; ʾāmîr 'mountain top' here against 'uppermost bough' at 17:6 (recorded departure: the image moves from tree to landscape); 'their strong cities' (ASV, NJPS) for the singular suffix. 17:10 'pleasant plants … strange slips' (ASV); the Adonis-gardens reading of naʿămānîm reported in a labelled comparative paragraph only, and the central dumuzi-tammuz-adonis-dying-and-rising-vegetation-god-cross-corpus deliberately NOT applied, since the line names no god. 17:11 tᵉśaḡśēḡî 'you make it grow' (JPS 1917, KJV, NJPS; ASV 'hedgest it in' in commentary); nēḏ qāṣîr 'the harvest shall be a heap' (MT pointing, KJV, JPS 1917; ASV 'fleeth away' and NJPS 'wither away' in commentary); naḥălāh 'grief' (Niphal participle of ḥlh). 17:12 root repetition kept, 'uproar … roar … roaring', 'rushing … rush … rushing' (ASV). 17:13 galgal 'whirling dust' (ASV, JPS 1917); sûp̄āh 'storm' here against 'whirlwind' at 5:28 and 29:6 (recorded departure); the singular bô rendered 'them'. 17:14 singular ʾênennû rendered 'they are no more' (ASV); bzz 'plunder', as at 10:2, 6; 13:16; 24:3.
entries.rationale: Each item is a site the Translator flagged where the Hebrew is rare, obscure or open to two construals. The Editor keeps the Masoretic text and a standard public-domain rendering in every line, and the commentary reports the alternatives with their sources. Two items in 17:11 change the Translator's ASV wording, and each follows a reference version. (a) The Pilpel tᵉśaḡśēḡî stands in synonymous parallel with taprîḥî 'you make blossom'. JPS 1917, KJV and NJPS read 'make grow'; ASV alone derives it from śûḡ 'fence about'. (b) As pointed, nēḏ is the noun 'heap' (Exod 15:8; Josh 3:13, 16; Ps 33:7; 78:13), which KJV and JPS 1917 follow. The verb nwd, read by ASV and NJPS, would normally give nāḏ, so keeping the pointing applies mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah. Two items depart from a concordance default, and the reasons are recorded here. At 17:9, ʾāmîr follows ASV 'mountain top' because the image there is a landscape of abandoned sites (NJPS treats both nouns as names). At 17:13, sûp̄āh keeps ASV 'storm', so that 'whirling dust before the whirlwind' is avoided; the concordance rules make only kāḇôḏ 'glory' strict. At 17:3 the accents (athnach on ʾărām) support ASV's construal, and JPS 1917 and NJPS's subject reading gives the same sense. At 17:5 the toponym is kept apart from the common noun rᵉp̄āʾîm 'shades / giants', because Josh 15:8 and 2 Sam 5:18, 22 locate a valley of that name near Jerusalem. At 17:10 the reading 'plantings of Adonis' is a history-of-religions hypothesis held by several commentators. The Hebrew names no god, and ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all render the adjective, so it belongs in labelled commentary and not in the line or the glossaryRefs. No item adopts a Wheel of Heaven reading, so the claim type is direct. Post-review refinement at 17:2: the Hebrew separates the feminine tihyeynāh (the cities) from the masculine wᵉrāḇᵉṣû (the flocks), so the line takes ASV and JPS 1917's 'which shall lie down' instead of 'and they shall lie down', which blurred the referent.

entries.strongs: H3568 (Kûš). Number from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: kûš, the land and people of the Nile valley south of Egypt (Nubia; the kingdom of Kush)
entries.literal: Cush
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'Cush' (11:11) but 'Ethiopia' elsewhere (18:1; 20:3-5; 43:3; 45:14); JPS 1917 'Cush' (11:11), 'Ethiopia' elsewhere; NJPS 'Nubia' throughout Isaiah (but 'Cush' at Gen 10:6); Koren 'Kush'; LXX Αἰθιοπία
entries.wohChoice: 'Cush' for kûš throughout Isaiah, for the land and for the people as a collective: 11:11 'from Pathros and from Cush'; 18:1 'beyond the rivers of Cush'; 20:3 'upon Egypt and upon Cush'; 20:4 'the exiles of Cush'; 20:5 'Cush their expectation'; 43:3 'Cush and Seba'; 45:14 'the merchandise of Cush'. Expected site: 37:9 'Tirhakah king of Cush' (the same name in 2 Kgs 19:9); add ISA-37:9 to appliesTo once chapter 37 is drafted. Never 'Ethiopia'. ASV/JPS 1917 'Ethiopia' and NJPS 'Nubia' are given in commentary. The phrase mēʿēḇer lᵉnahărê-ḵûš (18:1; cf. Zeph 3:10) is 'beyond the rivers of Cush'.
entries.rationale: Kûš is the Hebrew name of the Nile lands south of the first cataract, the kingdom Egyptian texts call Kush. In Isaiah's lifetime its kings ruled Egypt as the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, and they are the background most commentators assume for chapters 18 and 20. The English 'Ethiopia' comes through the LXX Αἰθιοπία and the Vulgate. Today it names a different country on the Ethiopian highlands, so it misplaces the referent for most readers. ASV is not consistent here: it prints 'Cush' at 11:11 and 'Ethiopia' at 18:1, 20:3-5, 43:3 and 45:14, and JPS 1917 has the same split (all checked 2026-11-26). NJPS uses the geographical 'Nubia' in Isaiah but the name 'Cush' at Gen 10:6 (Sefaria, checked). The book already prints 'Cush' at the signed-off 11:11, 43:3 and 45:14, and wave I-4 ruling 12 fixes the form for chapters 18 and 20. One entry therefore anchors the name book-wide, as aram-names-isaiah does for Aram. The choice is the Hebrew name in its standard English spelling. It carries no interpretation, so the claim is direct. Cross-corpus note: the Torah translations print the transliterated 'Kush' (genesis-woh 2:13; 10:6-8, beside 'Mitsrayim'). That follows the Torah transliteration convention, while Isaiah follows the wave rulings on English names. A central entry is recommended only if the founder wants one form across the corpus. The gentilic kûšî 'Cushite' (e.g. Jer 13:23), if it occurs in a later chapter, should take 'Cushite' under this entry.

entries.strongs: H6767 (ṣᵉlāṣal / ṣilṣal); H3671 (kānāp̄); H776 (ʾereṣ). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: ṣilṣal 'whirring, buzzing' (reduplicated noun of the sound-imitating root ṣll) in construct with the dual kᵉnāp̄āyim 'wings'
entries.partOfSpeech: construct phrase (noun + dual noun) in apposition to the vocative 'land'
entries.literal: land of the whirring of two wings / of wings
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'the land of the rustling of wings'; JPS 1917 'land of the buzzing of wings'; KJV 'the land shadowing with wings'; NJPS 'land in the deep shadow of wings' (note: 'Or "Most sheltered land"'); Koren 'land of buzzing wings'; LXX γῆς πλοίων πτέρυγες 'wings of ships'; NRSV 'whirring wings' (not verified)
entries.wohChoice: 'land of the rustling of wings' (ASV) at 18:1. The dual is rendered simply as 'wings', and the line names no referent: not insects, armies, ships or anything else. The options (insect wings, the noise of an army, shadow, sails) and their sources are given in commentary. Any Wheel of Heaven reading is confined to a final commentary paragraph labelled speculative (wave I-4 ruling 9).
entries.rationale: The phrase is the lens-salient crux of Isaiah 18, so it gets its own entry. The entry fixes a line that is philological and free of any referent. Ṣilṣal is a reduplicated noun of the root ṣll 'to tingle, quiver, whir'. The same consonants name a whirring locust at Deut 28:42 and a fish-spear at Job 40:31, and the related ṣelṣᵉlîm are cymbals (2 Sam 6:5; Ps 150:5). BDB s.v. ṣilṣāl gives 'land of buzzing of (insects') wings (so prob.)'. BDB s.v. kānāp̄ refers the phrase to the swarms of flies of the Nile lands (after Duhm and Cheyne) and records three other views: Knobel and Dillmann on the tropical shadow falling both ways, Gesenius's Thesaurus on the noise of an army's wings, and the sails of the boats of 18:2. BDB judges that the sails view 'would be suitable, but ṣilṣal does not favour this' (BDB checked via Sefaria's lexicon, 2026-11-26). The shadow reading (KJV; NJPS, with its note 'Or "Most sheltered land"') derives the word from ṣēl 'shade'. The sails reading is the LXX's πλοίων πτέρυγες (LXX text checked on getbible.net). ASV 'rustling of wings' renders the sound-word and the noun and adds no referent. It is the public-domain baseline, close to JPS 1917 'buzzing' and to the lexical gloss, so it is kept. Rendering the dual as plain 'wings' follows all the English versions, since the dual of paired body parts does not mean 'two' in English. The choice is the standard rendering, so the claim is direct. The interpretive options belong to commentary, and a reading that makes the wings mechanical belongs only in a labelled speculative note. The canon does not cite the verse (TBWTT and the other canon books in data-library checked 2026-11-26).

entries.lemma: qaw 'cord, measuring line', reduplicated in the epithet qaw-qāw (18:2, 7) and in the taunt qaw lāqāw (28:10, 13)
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (masculine), reduplicated; with mᵉḇûsāh 'trampling' (noun of bws)
entries.literal: a nation of line-line and trampling
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'a nation that meteth out and treadeth down' (18:2, 7), 'line upon line' (28:10, 13); KJV 'a nation meted out and trodden down'; JPS 1917 'a nation that is sturdy and treadeth down', 'line by line'; Koren 'a nation mighty and conquering'; NJPS 'a nation of gibber and chatter' (note 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain; cf. 28.10'), 'mutter upon mutter, murmur upon murmur' (28:10); BDB 'a mighty nation' (qawqāw 'might (?)', 'so read (according to most)', Arabic quwwa); LXX ἔθνος ἀνέλπιστον (18:2), ἐλπίδα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι (28:10)
entries.wohChoice: 18:2, 7: 'a nation that measures out and treads down' (ASV, modernized). The 'line' reading is kept, and the epithet is rendered the same way at both sites. 28:10, 13 (when drafted): default 'line upon line', with the same 'line' derivation, so that the two passages stay consistent. If the chapter 28 Editor adopts a different construal there (unintelligible speech with NJPS, or 'hope' with the LXX), that Editor must revisit 18:2, 7 in the same pass or escalate the split. Other occurrences of qaw as the measuring line (28:17; 34:11, 17; 44:13) take 'line'. Settled by the chapter 28 Editor (wave I-5): 28:10, 13 'precept upon precept, precept upon precept, line upon line, line upon line, here a little, there a little' (ASV, Koren; JPS 1917 'precept by precept … line by line'), with ṣaw taken from ṣwh 'command' ('precept') and qaw from 'line'; 28:17 'I will make justice the line'. 18:2, 7 therefore stand unchanged. The NJPS sound-imitation reading ('mutter upon mutter, murmur upon murmur') and the LXX 'hope' derivation are given in commentary at 28:10, 13.
entries.rationale: Qaw is the builder's or surveyor's line (BDB: 2 Kgs 21:13; Isa 34:11, 17; 44:13; Job 38:5). The reduplicated qaw-qāw occurs only in the epithet of the distant nation at 18:2, 7 and, as qaw lāqāw, in the drunkards' taunt at 28:10, 13. Three construals compete. (1) From 'line': the nation 'measures out' (KJV, ASV), that is, it marks off conquered land with the line, as the line is stretched over a city for destruction (2 Kgs 21:13; Isa 34:11). (2) From a homonym 'strength', compared with Arabic quwwa: 'mighty' (BDB, which says most interpreters read so; JPS 1917 'sturdy'; Koren 'mighty'). (3) A sound-word for foreign speech: NJPS 'gibber and chatter', which ties the epithet explicitly to 28:10, where NJPS has 'mutter upon mutter', and to the motif of the nation of unintelligible speech (33:19; Deut 28:49; Jer 5:15). The LXX shows a fourth, older construal: it derives both passages from qwh 'to hope' (ἀνέλπιστον; ἐλπίδα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι, checked on getbible.net). The line keeps construal (1). It is the reading of the public-domain baseline, it rests on the attested noun rather than on a postulated homonym, and it matches the ASV wording of 28:10. It is not the lexical majority, though, and BDB's 'might' is a serious alternative, so the claim is inferred rather than direct. The entry exists so that 18:2, 7 and 28:10, 13 are decided together: whatever the chapter 28 Editor rules, the two passages share a reduplicated form and should share a derivation. Mᵉḇûsāh 'trampling' (bws, Isa 22:5 'treading down') is rendered verbally, 'treads down', with ASV. Wave I-5 (chapter 28 Editor): the forward commitment is kept, so 18:2, 7 need no revisit and nothing is escalated. ṣaw: BDB s.v. ṣaw (checked via Sefaria's lexicon, 2026-11-26) calls the word dubious and records three views: 'command upon command' (Gesenius, Cheyne; AV, RV), the carpenter's 'rule' paired with the 'line' (Ewald, Dillmann), and 'mocking sounds without sense' (Duhm, Cheyne); BDB s.v. qaw refers 28:10, 13 to the same discussion and lists 28:17 under the measuring line. 'Precept' (ASV, KJV, Koren; JPS 1917 'precept by precept') keeps the lexical-noun construal on which this entry rests. NJPS 'mutter upon mutter, murmur upon murmur' (checked) represents the sound-imitation view, which many modern scholars hold; it is given full weight in the 28:10 commentary, with the LXX θλῖψιν ἐπὶ θλῖψιν … ἐλπίδα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι (checked). The claim stays inferred. Wave I-5: the measuring-line clause applied at 34:11 (qaw-tōhû 'the line of wasteland', with ʾaḇnê-ḇōhû 'the plummet of emptiness') and 34:17 (baq-qāw 'by line'), as the wohChoice provides. The reduplicated forms at 28:10, 13 are left to the chapter-28 Editor.

entries.lemma: single-site lexical and syntactic decisions of Isaiah 18
entries.literal: the one sending envoys in the sea; vessels of papyrus; go, messengers; drawn out and made smooth; feared from it and onward; (rivers) divide; you will see … you will hear; like dazzling heat upon light; like a cloud of dew; he removed, he cut down; bird of prey; upon it; a gift will be brought … a people
entries.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; alternatives from JPS 1917, NJPS (1985), KJV, Koren and the LXX recorded in commentary
entries.wohChoice: 18:2 'which sends envoys by the sea, and in vessels of papyrus upon the face of the waters!' (ASV 'ambassadors'; the water is not identified as the Nile); no supplied '[saying]' before 'Go, you swift messengers'; 'a nation tall and smooth' (ASV); 'a people feared from their beginning onward' (ASV temporal construal, 'feared' for ASV 'terrible'); 'whose land the rivers divide' (ASV). 18:3 imperfects as imperatives, 'see … hear!' (ASV, NJPS); impersonal infinitives without a supplied subject. 18:4 ASV similes 'like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew'; 'I will look on in my dwelling place'. 18:5 MT 'harvest' (not the emended 'vintage'); asyndeton kept, 'he will take away, he will cut down'; the subject 'he' left unnamed. 18:6 ʿêṭ 'the ravenous birds' (ASV, JPS 1917); singular ʿālāyw rendered 'upon them' (ASV). 18:7 'a gift' for šay; MT without a preposition before the first ʿam, so 'a people tall and smooth' stands in apposition to the gift; 'to the place of the name of YHWH of hosts, Mount Zion' (literal). Epithets repeated from 18:2 are rendered identically.
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator flagged a choice among standard renderings. The Editor keeps the Masoretic text and the ASV baseline unless a concordance rule requires otherwise, and records the alternatives in commentary. The renderings rest on the lexica: ṣîr 'envoy' (BDB: 'envoy, from Cush Is 18:2'); gōmeʾ 'papyrus, paper-reed' (BDB: 'vessels of paper-reed', as in the basket of Exod 2:3); mᵉmuššāḵ, the Pual of mšk, 'of persons, = tall' (BDB); bāzāʾ 'divide, cut through', compared with Aramaic bᵉzaʿ (BDB); šay 'gift offered as homage' (BDB; Ps 68:30; 76:12). All were checked via Sefaria's BDB, 2026-11-26. Three choices depart from ASV wording, and none changes the sense. (a) 'feared' for nôrāʾ, the Niphal participle of yrʾ 'fear', because ASV 'terrible' now usually means 'very bad'. The chapter 21 draft keeps 'terrible' for the feminine nôrāʾāh of a land (21:1); the orchestrator may harmonize. (b) 'and in vessels' for ASV 'even in vessels'. (c) no supplied '[saying]', so that the unintroduced imperative stands as in the Hebrew. NJPS's reordering of 18:2 and its '[Say this:]' at 18:3 are recorded, and NJPS's note that haššōlēaḥ agrees with 'nation', not with the feminine 'land', is reported. At 18:4 the NJPS readings ('rest calm and confident' from hibbîṭ 'rely'; 'scorching heat upon sprouts' with ʾôr as 'herb', as KJV 'upon herbs'; 'rain-cloud') and the LXX's 'day of harvest' (which presupposes bᵉyôm) are reported and not adopted. At 18:5 NJPS's 'Emendation yields "vintage"' is reported and MT is kept. At 18:7 ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS supply 'from' or 'of' before the first ʿam, and the LXX has ἐκ λαοῦ. MT has no preposition there, and the line keeps MT under mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah. None of these choices carries a lens.

entries.strongs: H7392 (rāḵaḇ 'ride'); H5645 (ʿāḇ 'cloud, cloud-mass'); H7031 (qal 'light, swift'). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: rōḵēḇ, Qal participle of rāḵaḇ 'ride, be mounted'; ʿāḇ 'dense cloud, cloud-mass'; qal 'light, swift'
entries.partOfSpeech: predicate participle with prepositional phrase (noun + adjective)
entries.literal: behold, YHWH riding upon a light cloud
entries.standardEnglish: Behold, Jehovah rideth upon a swift cloud (ASV); the LORD rideth upon a swift cloud (JPS 1917); Mounted on a swift cloud, the LORD will come (NJPS); super nubem levem (Vulgate); epi nephelēs kouphēs (LXX; recalled)
entries.wohChoice: 'Behold, YHWH rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt' (19:1): present tense for the predicate participle; lower-case 'cloud'; 'swift' for qal (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS), with the 'light' of the Vulgate and LXX in commentary. No epithet ('Rider of the Clouds') in the line. The Ugaritic and Hebrew storm-theophany background is given in commentary under the central rider-of-the-clouds entry. Any Wheel of Heaven reading appears only in a final commentary paragraph labelled speculative (wave I-4 ruling 9). ʿāḇ is 'cloud' like ʿānān (4:5), and commentary names the Hebrew noun where the distinction matters.
entries.rationale: Isa 19:1 is the book's one use of the cloud-riding image, and it is lens-salient, so the rendering is fixed in its own entry for audit. The participle rōḵēḇ after hinnēh is predicative, and the standard English versions render it in the present ('rideth', 'mounted'), as the line does. ʿāḇ is the thick cloud-mass (BDB), as in Ps 104:3 ('who makes the clouds his chariot'), and qal is 'light', hence 'swift' (BDB). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all print 'swift cloud' (checked on Sefaria and bible-api.com, 2026-11-26). The image belongs to the West Semitic storm-theophany idiom: Ugaritic rkb ʿrpt 'Rider of the Clouds', the epithet of Baʿlu (project edition, KTU 1.2 iv 6; 1.3 ii 40; 1.3 iv 23; 1.4 vi 10), and the Hebrew rōḵēḇ bāʿărāḇôṯ (Ps 68:5) and rōḵēḇ šāmayim (Deut 33:26). Isaiah uses a clause with a singular noun and an adjective, not the title. The line therefore translates the clause and does not print an epithet. The canon does not cite Isa 19 (checked against the data-library texts of The Book Which Tells the Truth and Extraterrestrials Took Me to Their Planet, 2026-11-26). Its readings of the cloud at 1 Kgs 8:12 and Job 37:18 as craft (TBWTT 3:107; 3:259-260) are reported in a labelled speculative paragraph only. The rendering is the consensus one, so the claim is direct.

entries.strongs: H5892 (ʿîr); H2041 (heres 'destruction'); cf. H2775 (ḥeres 'sun'), the variant. Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: heres 'destruction' (from hāras 'tear down'), found only here; variant ḥeres 'sun'
entries.partOfSpeech: construct noun phrase used as a place-name
entries.literal: city of the destruction; it shall be said to one
entries.standardEnglish: The city of destruction (ASV, JPS 1917); Town of Heres (NJPS, with the note 'Many Heb. mss. read ḥeres, "sun"'); civitas Solis (Vulgate; recalled); polis asedek (LXX, as if ʿîr haṣṣedeq; recalled)
entries.wohChoice: 'one shall be called the City of Destruction' (19:18): MT in the line (wave I-4 ruling 5; overlay mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah). Commentary gives the variant ḥeres 'sun' (many Hebrew manuscripts; reported for 1QIsaᵃ), its link to Heliopolis/On and Jer 43:13 bêṯ šemeš, the Targum's 'Beth Shemesh' as reported by NJPS, the Vulgate and LXX readings, and the proposal that MT is a deliberate alteration, without deciding it. Capitalised as a name.
entries.rationale: The Masoretic Text reads ʿîr haheres, and ASV and JPS 1917 render it 'The city of destruction' (checked). The book's textual policy translates MT and reports the variants of the Great Isaiah Scroll and the ancient versions in commentary (overlay mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah), and wave I-4 ruling 5 applies that policy to this verse by name. The variant ḥeres 'sun' differs by one letter (ḥ for h) and is attested in many Hebrew manuscripts, according to the NJPS note (checked). It is also reported for 1QIsaᵃ (not checked against DJD 32). It would identify the city as Heliopolis, the Hebrew On (central on-heliopolis-egyptian-toponym), called bêṯ šemeš at Jer 43:13. The Vulgate (civitas Solis) and the LXX (polis asedek, 'city of righteousness') are recalled, not checked against an edition. Commentators often explain MT as a polemical alteration connected with the Jewish temple at Leontopolis (Josephus, Antiquities 13.62-73; recalled). Others defend MT as original. The entry records the evidence without ruling on it. The line renders MT literally, so the claim is direct, although the meaning of heres, a word found only here, remains uncertain (NJPS 'Meaning uncertain').

entries.lemma: single-site lexical decisions of Isaiah 19
entries.partOfSpeech: nouns, verbs, participles, particles and construct phrases
entries.literal: Egypt against Egypt … a man against his brother; be emptied; I will swallow; the soft-speakers (?); hard lords; the sea / a river; Nile-channels of Mazor; stink; reed and rush; bare places (?); at the mouth of the Nile; white stuff; her foundations; hire; sad of soul; counsel / to counsel; your wise ones; Noph; the corner of her tribes; a spirit of twistings; go astray / stagger; the waving of the hand / waving; terror; a savior and one who contends; be known; serve sacrifice and offering; serve … with Assyria; a third; which he blessed him; blessed my people Egypt
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: the Egyptians against the Egyptians … every one against his brother; shall fail; I will destroy the counsel thereof; the charmers; a cruel lord; the sea / the river; the streams of Egypt; become foul; the reeds and flags; the meadows; by the brink of the Nile; white cloth; the pillars [of Egypt]; work for hire; grieved in soul; counsel / purposed, purpose; thy wise men; Memphis; that are the corner-stone of her tribes; a spirit of perverseness; go astray / staggereth; the shaking of the hand / shaketh; a terror; a saviour, and a defender; shall be known; worship with sacrifice and oblation; worship with the Assyrians; the third; for that … hath blessed them; Blessed be Egypt my people. NJPS (checked): Egyptian against Egyptian; drained of spirit; confound its plans; the shades; a harsh master; the seas / rivers; Egypt's canals; turn foul; the Nile papyrus; chagrined; her foundations / all who make dams; your sages; Tanis / Memphis; the chiefs of her tribes; a spirit of distortion; will raise His hand; the dread; a savior and champion; will make Himself known; serve [Him] with sacrifice and oblation; together with the Assyrians shall serve [the LORD]; a third partner; will bless them; Blessed be My people Egypt
entries.wohChoice: 19:2 'Egyptians against Egyptians' (ASV), the one place where miṣrayim is rendered as the people, because the reciprocal fighting needs persons; elsewhere in the chapter 'Egypt' wherever the Hebrew has the name, with the pronoun the Hebrew gives (vv. 4, 16, 21, 23 keep 'Egypt' where ASV has 'the Egyptians'); distributive ʾîš 'everyone … his'. 19:3 'shall be emptied' for the Niphal of bqq (JPS 1917; as 24:3), with 'fail' kept for nšt in v5; ʾăḇallēaʿ 'I will destroy' (blʿ I, as 3:12; 9:15); hāʾiṭṭîm 'the charmers' (ASV), not 'the shades' (reserved for rᵉp̄āʾîm) and not 'ghosts' (ʾōḇôṯ in the same list). 19:4 ʾăḏōnîm qāšeh 'a cruel lord' (ASV, JPS 1917). 19:5 hayyām 'the sea' and nāhār 'the river' (the Nile), with the capital 'the River' kept for hannāhār = Euphrates (8:7; 11:15). 19:6 yᵉʾōrê māṣôr 'the streams of Egypt' (ASV; māṣôr as a poetic name of Egypt); heʾeznîḥû 'become foul'; qāneh wāsûp̄ 'reed and rush'. 19:7 ʿārôṯ 'the meadows' (ASV); ʿal-pî yᵉʾôr 'by the brink of the Nile'. 19:9 ḥôrāy 'white cloth' (ASV; MT vowels). 19:10 MT kept: 'her pillars … all who work for hire shall be grieved in soul'; ASV's supplied '[of Egypt]' dropped. 19:3, 11, 12, 17 ʿēṣāh / yāʿaṣ: 'counsel' for human advice (vv. 3, 11), 'purpose / purposed / purposes' for YHWH's plan (vv. 12, 17), following ASV and the stable 14:24-27. 19:11-12 ḥăḵāmîm 'the wise' where generic (v11), 'your wise men' for Pharaoh's court sages (v12; scope ruling 13; as stable 29:14). Founder ruling 2026-11-26: 'your wise men' stands, ruling 13 covering a specific professional class as well as military groups; NJPS 'your sages' is reported in commentary. 19:13 nōp̄ 'Memphis' (ASV; ruling 4); pinnaṯ šᵉḇāṭêhā in apposition to the subject: 'those who are the cornerstone of her tribes have led Egypt astray' (ASV construal). 19:14 rûaḥ ʿiwʿîm 'a spirit of perverseness' (ASV), lower case; tʿh 'lead astray' (Hiphil) / 'stagger' (Hithpael). 19:16 tᵉnûp̄aṯ yāḏ … mēnîp̄ 'the waving of the hand … which he waves', as 11:15 'wave his hand'; kannāšîm 'like women' literal. 19:17 lᵉḥāggāʾ 'a terror'. 19:20 mōšîaʿ wārāḇ 'a savior and a defender' (ASV; rāḇ from rîḇ), lower case. 19:21 wᵉnôḏaʿ 'shall be known' (passive, ASV); ʿāḇaḏ + offering 'worship with'. 19:23 ʾeṯ = 'with': 'Egypt shall worship with Assyria'. 19:24 šᵉlîšiyyāh 'the third' (ASV). 19:25 ʾăšer bērăḵô 'whom … has blessed' (relative; singular suffix); 'Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance' (ASV order; Hebrew order in commentary).
entries.rationale: Each item is a single-site decision that keeps a standard rendering. The choice between ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (all checked on Sefaria and bible-api.com, 2026-11-26) is made on lexical grounds, and the alternative is recorded in commentary, so one entry governs the chapter's cruxes, as lexical-cruxes-isaiah-10 does for chapter 10. Three items change the draft line, and the entry records why. (1) 19:3 'shall be emptied' replaces ASV 'shall fail' because the verb is bqq 'empty out' (BDB; JPS 1917 'made empty'), the stem and root of 24:3, and because 'fail' renders a different verb, nšt, two verses later. (2) 19:13 follows the ASV construal of pinnaṯ šᵉḇāṭêhā as apposition to the subject (cf. pinnôṯ kol-hāʿām 'the chiefs of all the people', Judg 20:2); the draft's order made the phrase appear to describe Egypt, the very entity whose tribes it names. (3) 19:7-8 'the Nile' for singular yᵉʾôr follows wave I-4 ruling 15 (the context clause on central yeor-nile-egyptian-loanword is carried by the chapter 23 Editor). This entry records only the companion decision for nāhār at 19:5 ('the river', lower case, distinct from the capitalised Euphrates 'the River' of 8:7 and 11:15). The remaining items keep the draft. The concordance rules of the book are applied: ʾăḏāmāh 'ground' (central adam-adamah) at 19:17; the hiphil of nûp̄ 'wave' as at 11:15; blʿ I 'destroy' as at 3:12 and 9:15; YHWH's ʿēṣāh 'purpose' as in the stable 14:24-27; 'shades' reserved for rᵉp̄āʾîm (overlay rephaim-shades-dead-isaiah-26). The gender-neutral rule for generic human nouns (overlay adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah) is applied within its scope ruling (wave I-4 ruling 13). The distributive ʾîš of 19:2 is 'everyone', the generic sense. ḥăḵāmêḵā at 19:12 names a specific body, Pharaoh's court sages, and keeps 'wise men', as the stable 29:14 does (founder ruling 2026-11-26 on the scope of ruling 13; NJPS 'your sages' in commentary). Hapaxes and uncertain words (ʾiṭṭîm, heʾeznîḥû, ʿārôṯ, ḥôrāy, šāṯōṯêhā, ʿiwʿîm, ḥāggāʾ) keep ASV, and the lexical alternatives are recorded (HALOT's comparison of ʾiṭṭîm with Akkadian eṭemmu 'spirit of the dead' is recalled; NJPS 'the shades' checked). None of the items carries a lens, and every rendering is that of at least one standard version, except 19:16 'waving … waves', which follows the book's concordance with 11:15 (Hiphil nûp̄, BDB 'wave, brandish'), so the claim is direct.

(ASV).
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator flagged a choice among standard renderings. The Editor keeps the Masoretic Text and the public-domain baseline unless accuracy or the book's concordance requires a change, and records the alternatives in commentary. No item adopts an emendation or carries a project reading. Two English lines change. (1) At 20:1 tartān is the Assyrian military title turtānu 'commander-in-chief' (CAD T s.v. turtānu, recalled; also 2 Kgs 18:17). This is the scholarly consensus, and NJPS prints 'the Tartan' with an explanatory note. ASV's bare 'Tartan' reads in modern English as a personal name and misinforms the reader, so the line supplies the article. The Hebrew omits it, as it does with other foreign titles used like names (rab-šāqēh, 2 Kgs 18:17). When 2 Kgs 18:17 is drafted it should follow the same rule. (2) At 20:3 the draft's 'upon Egypt and upon Cush' was reported as ASV but is the wording of JPS 1917. ASV reads 'concerning', which states the sense of ʿal here (the referent of the sign) in current English, so the line takes ASV. Other attributions in the draft were also corrected after checking: 'ashamed' at 20:5 is JPS 1917 (ASV 'confounded'), and the quotation extent 20:3-6, with an inner quotation at 20:6, matches both JPS 1917 and NJPS. The remaining items keep the Translator's line. 'Sandals' treats the singular naʿal as a collective (cf. Josh 5:15) and keeps the book's word at 5:27. ʿārôm is kept as 'naked' in all three occurrences, the rendering of all three references, and the 'scantily clad' sense (1 Sam 19:24; Mic 1:8) is reported. The ʾaṯnāḥ on wᵉyāḥēp̄ makes 'three years' grammatically part of the sign clause. The ambiguous ASV order is kept and the JPS 1917 accent-following rendering is reported. ʿerwaṯ miṣrāyim is rendered by its sense, 'to the shame of Egypt', in all three references, so the central ervat-aviv entry (Gen 9 idiom) is not extended. mabbāṭ is rendered concordantly in 20:5 and 20:6 so that the repetition stays visible.

entries.lemma: the watch vocabulary of Isaiah 21 (roots ṣph and šmr)
entries.partOfSpeech: Piel participle used as noun; nouns; Qal participle used as noun; infinitive absolute + hapax noun
entries.literal: one who looks out; a look-out place; my place of guarding; one who guards; to watch the watch(?)
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: watchman (21:6) … watch-tower … my ward (21:8) … Watchman (21:11-12); set the watch (21:5). JPS 1917: a watchman; the watch-tower; my ward; Watchman; light the lamps (21:5). NJPS: a sentry; my Lord's lookout; my post; Watchman; 'Let the watchman watch!' (21:5). NRSV (not verified): sentinel; watchtower; my post; Sentinel; spread the rugs (21:5).
entries.wohChoice: 21:6 ham-mᵉṣappeh 'the lookout'; 21:8 miṣpeh 'the watchtower' and mišmartî 'my post'; 21:11-12 šōmēr 'Watchman' / 'The watchman' (wave ruling 6); 21:5 ṣāp̄ōh haṣ-ṣāp̄îṯ 'they set the watch' (ASV), the hapax ṣāp̄îṯ kept in its watch sense, with the 'rugs' and 'lamps' readings in commentary.
entries.rationale: Isaiah 21 uses two different nouns for the figure who watches. ham-mᵉṣappeh (21:6), a Piel participle of ṣph 'look out, keep watch' (BDB), is the one posted to see and report ('let him declare what he sees'). šōmēr (21:11-12), the participle of šmr 'guard, keep', is the guard asked about the night. ASV and JPS 1917 give 'watchman' for both and so hide the change of word. Wave ruling 6 asks for a consistent watch vocabulary within the chapter, and the line now keeps one English word per Hebrew noun: 'lookout' for mᵉṣappeh (NJPS 'sentry' and NRSV 'sentinel' show that the modern versions also separate it) and the ruled 'Watchman' for šōmēr. The places follow the standard renderings, miṣpeh 'watchtower' (ASV, JPS 1917) and mišmeret 'post' (NJPS; ASV 'ward'). 'Watchtower' shares an English stem with 'watchman' although the roots differ, and this is accepted because 'lookout tower' would be unidiomatic and NJPS's bare 'lookout' would be confused with the person. At 21:5 the hapax ṣāp̄îṯ is uncertain: ASV and NJPS take it as watch or watchman, JPS 1917 as lamps, and several lexicons and NRSV as rugs. The line keeps ASV and the commentary reports the alternatives, so nothing in the line depends on the root link. The entry is scoped to this chapter. Later Isaiah sites with the Qal participle ṣōp̄eh (52:8; 56:10) and šōmᵉrîm (62:6) are left to their Editors, who should keep or explicitly drop the same distinction. The choices are standard and carry no lens.

entries.lemma: bāḡaḏ / šāḏaḏ participle pairs
entries.literal: the one dealing treacherously deals treacherously, and the one devastating devastates
entries.standardEnglish: the treacherous man dealeth treacherously, and the destroyer destroyeth (ASV); The treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth (JPS 1917); The betrayer is betraying, The ravager ravaging (NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the treacherous one deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys' at 21:2: the bgd family 'treacherous … deal treacherously' of the stable 24:16, in the present tense because both members are participles; šôḏēḏ 'the destroyer' as in the chapter-16 draft at 16:4.
entries.rationale: The bgd paronomasia recurs in Isaiah at 21:2, 24:16 and 33:1, and a reader should be able to recognise it across chapters. The stable 24:16 renders the finite forms 'The treacherous have dealt treacherously; in treachery the treacherous have dealt treacherously' (overlay razi-li-pining-secret-crux-isaiah-24), so this entry fixes the same English family, 'treacherous / deal treacherously', for 21:2, with the tense following the Hebrew form: participle plus participle gives the present. ASV and JPS 1917 use the same family, so the choice is the PD baseline and not a new reading. NJPS's 'betrayer is betraying' was considered and rejected because it would break the concordance with 24:16. The NJPS note reports an emendation to passives ('betrayed … ravaged'), comparing 33:1. MT is kept under mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah. šôḏēḏ is 'the destroyer' (ASV), as the chapter-16 draft prints at 16:4 (mippᵉnê šôḏēḏ 'from the face of the destroyer'). JPS 1917 'spoiler' and NJPS 'ravager' are in commentary. When 33:1 is drafted its Editor should extend this entry. ISA-24:16 is not added to appliesTo here, because that stable chapter is outside this Editor's remit. The orchestrator may add it at merge with no change to the line. Wave I-5 (Isa 33): extended to 33:1 as the entry asked. The forms are vocative participles with second-person address and finite verbs, so the line reads 'Woe to you, destroyer, who were not destroyed, and treacherous one, with whom they did not deal treacherously! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have made an end of dealing treacherously, they will deal treacherously with you' (ASV 'destroyest … dealest treacherously'; JPS 1917 'spoilest'; NJPS 'ravager … betrayer'; all checked 2026-11-26). The hapax kannᵉlōṯᵉḵā is read with ASV ('made an end', klh); JPS 1917 'weary' (lʾh) is in commentary.

entries.lemma: proper names and region names of Isaiah 21
entries.partOfSpeech: proper nouns; common nouns used as region names
entries.literal: wilderness of sea; in the south (dry land); Elam; Media / the Medes; Babylon; Dumah ('silence'); Seir; in Arabia / in the steppe; Dedanites; Tema; Kedar
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: the wilderness of the sea; in the South; O Elam; O Media; Babylon; Dumah; Seir; upon Arabia; Dedanites; Tema; Kedar. NJPS: 'Desert of the Sea'; the Negeb; Elam; Media; Babylon; 'Dumah'; Seir; 'In the Steppe'; Dedanites; Tema; Kedar.
entries.wohChoice: 'the wilderness of the sea' (21:1, wave ruling 6) with no region named in the line; bannegeḇ 'in the South' (ASV, JPS 1917; 'the Negeb' in commentary); 'O Elam … O Media' (21:2); 'Babylon' (21:9, ruling 4); 'Dumah' and 'Seir' (21:11, ruling 6); 'Arabia' for both baʿrāḇ (21:13; 'the steppe' in commentary); 'Dedanites', 'Tema', 'Kedar', 'the children of Kedar' (ASV spellings, ruling 4).
entries.rationale: Isaiah 21 is a sequence of short oracles headed by cryptic catchwords, and the names are where a translation is most tempted to explain. The line keeps the names as the Hebrew gives them. Identifications stay in commentary: the Sea-Land of southern Mesopotamia for midbar-yām (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; recalled, not verified), the Ishmaelite Dumah of Gen 25:14 (NJPS note), Edom for Seir, and the north-Arabian oases and tribes for Tema, Dedan and Kedar. māḏay is 'Media' here and 'the Medes' at the stable 13:17. The two sites differ in syntax and the renderings are consistent with that. At 13:17 the name is the object of mēʿîr and governs plural verbs (yaḥšōḇû, yaḥpᵉṣû), so it is the people. At 21:2 it is a vocative beside the country name Elam, where ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all print 'Media'. The rule is recorded here so that later sites follow it: 'the Medes' with plural agreement, 'Media' as the land or the vocative of a land. bannegeḇ is kept as 'in the South' (ASV, JPS 1917) because the article and the image of storms from the south fit the compass sense, and NJPS 'Negeb' is in commentary. baʿrāḇ is 'Arabia' at both occurrences of 21:13, following ASV and JPS 1917. The steppe reading (NJPS) and the LXX evidence for bāʿereḇ 'in the evening' are reported in commentary. The possible wordplay on dûmāh 'silence' is likewise reported and not put in the line. All renderings are attested in the PD baseline and carry no lens. Wave I-5 (Isa 30): negeḇ 'the South' also in the heading of 30:6 (ASV, JPS 1917), as at 21:1; 'the Negeb' in commentary.

entries.partOfSpeech: nouns, verbs, participles, infinitives absolute, construct phrases
entries.literal: a hard vision; all its/her sighing; I am bent from hearing; my heart has wandered; he has set for me; to arrange … to eat, to drink; chariotry/riders; a pair of horsemen; he will attend with attention, much attention; Lord/my lord; all the nights; a troop of men; he shattered; my threshed one and son of my threshing floor; turn, come; in the scrub/forest; bring!/they brought; with his bread; the heaviness of war; number of bow, mighty ones of
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: grievous vision; all the sighing thereof; I am pained so that I cannot hear; My heart fluttereth; hath been turned; They prepare the table … they eat, they drink; a troop; horsemen in pairs; he shall hearken diligently with much heed; O Lord; whole nights; a troop of men; are broken; O thou my threshing, and the grain of my floor; turn ye, come; In the forest; they brought water; with their bread; the grievousness of war; the number of the archers, the mighty men.
entries.wohChoice: 21:2 'A harsh vision' (NJPS; departs from ASV 'grievous'); 'All its sighing I have brought to an end' (ASV). 21:3 'I am bowed down so that I cannot hear' (ʿwh 'be bent'; JPS 1917 'bent'; departs from ASV 'pained'), min privative. 21:4 'My heart reels' (tʿh 'stagger'; departs from ASV 'fluttereth'); śām rendered passive, 'has been turned' (ASV, JPS 1917). 21:5 the infinitives absolute descriptive, 'They prepare the table …' (ASV). 21:7, 9 reḵeḇ 'a troop'; ṣemeḏ pārāšîm 'horsemen in pairs'; 'he shall listen diligently, with great attention'. 21:8 'O Lord' (MT pointing); kol-hallêlôṯ 'whole nights' (ASV). 21:9 reḵeḇ ʾîš 'a troop of men' (wave ruling 13); šibbar passive 'are broken'. 21:10 'O my threshing, and the grain of my threshing floor' (ASV). 21:12 'turn back, come'. 21:13 bayyaʿar 'In the thicket' (JPS 1917 'thickets'; departs from ASV 'forest'; yaʿar stays 'forest' elsewhere in Isaiah). 21:14 hêṯāyû imperative, 'To meet the thirsty bring water!' (JPS 1917 'bring ye water', NJPS 'Meet the thirsty with water'; founder ruling 2026-11-26; ASV's perfect 'they brought' in commentary); the second clause keeps the perfect qiddᵉmû with the inhabitants of Tema as its subject, as the accents require: 'The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitive with his bread.'; bᵉlaḥmô 'with his bread' (JPS 1917; departs from ASV 'their'). 21:15 kōḇeḏ 'the grievousness of war' (ASV). 21:17 'the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar' (ASV; wave ruling 13).
entries.rationale: Each item is a single-site decision between ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS, made on lexical or grammatical grounds, with the alternatives recorded in commentary. None carries a project reading. (1) Five departures from ASV restore the lexical sense of the Hebrew, each attested in a PD or modern Jewish version. At 21:2 qāšeh is 'hard, harsh' (BDB; NJPS 'harsh'), which also leaves 'grievous' for kōḇeḏ at 21:15. At 21:3 the Niphal of ʿwh is 'be bent, bowed' (JPS 1917 'bent'), not 'pained'. At 21:4 tʿh is 'wander, stagger' (28:7), and 'reels' keeps the image that ASV 'fluttereth' loses. At 21:13 yaʿar covers scrub and thicket (BDB), which the Arabian steppe requires (JPS 1917 'thickets', NJPS 'scrub'), while 'forest' remains the rendering for wooded sites such as 10:18 and 10:34. At 21:14 the suffix of bᵉlaḥmô is singular (JPS 1917 'with his bread'). (2) Where the Hebrew is ambiguous the ASV construal is kept, and the alternative is put in commentary. At 21:4 and 21:9 the active verbs śām and šibbar have no expressed subject, and the English passive is the standard rendering of such an indefinite subject (NJPS supplies 'He' at 21:4). At 21:5 the infinitives absolute may be description (ASV, JPS 1917) or quoted orders (NJPS). At 21:8 the vocative ʾăḏōnāy follows the MT pointing, and NJPS's alternative 'my lord' is reported. At 21:14 hêṯāyû may be imperative (JPS 1917, NJPS) or perfect (ASV), and here the line departs from ASV by founder ruling 2026-11-26: it reads the imperative. The identical form hêṯāyû at Jer 12:9 follows the imperatives lᵉḵû ʾispû and is itself an imperative (WLC, checked by the Reviewer and the Editor), and the main pause (atnach) at māyim closes the command with the first half of the verse. The following qiddᵉmû is pointed as a perfect and the accents make the inhabitants of Tema its subject, so the second clause stays a statement (ASV, JPS 1917), and ASV's perfect 'they brought' is reported in commentary. (3) Under wave ruling 13, ʾîš at 21:9 (a troop of riders) and gibbôrê at 21:17 name specific groups of warriors and keep 'men', as at the stable 13:3. The gender-neutral adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah is not applied. (4) The kbd root of kōḇeḏ (21:15) is not governed by the strict kāḇôḏ 'glory' concordance of wave ruling 2, which covers the noun kāḇôḏ (21:16) only.

entries.wohChoice: 22:1, 5 gêʾ ḥizzāyôn 'the valley of vision', lower case (ASV; wave ruling 7). 22:3 miqqešeṯ ʾussārû 'they were bound by the archers' (ASV; the privative 'without the bow' of JPS 1917 / NJPS in commentary). 22:4 baṯ-ʿammî 'the daughter of my people' (ASV, JPS 1917; the appositional sense in commentary); ʾāmartî past, 'Therefore I said'. 22:5 possessive lᵉ: 'For the Lord YHWH of hosts has a day of tumult …', concordant with 2:12 (NJPS; changed from the draft's ASV 'from the Lord'); mᵉqarqar qir wᵉšôaʿ ʾel-hāhār 'a breaking down of the wall, and a crying to the mountain', common nouns in MT's singular (Kir / Shoa as peoples, JPS 1917 / NJPS, in commentary). 22:6 'with chariots of men and horsemen' ('and' supplied, as ASV; ASV's supplied '[and say]' not added. 22:16 third-person suffixes kept with ASV alone, 'hewing out his tomb on high … for himself' (JPS 1917 and NJPS both convert to the second person); qeḇer 'tomb'. 22:17 'hurl you away violently, like a strong man; ʾăḏōneyḵā 'your lord', lower case. 22:19 yehersᵉḵā rendered as a passive, 'you shall be pulled down' (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS; MT third person in commentary). 22:21 kuttōneṯ 'robe', ʾaḇnēṭ 'girdle', memšālāh 'government' (ASV; NJPS 'tunic', 'sash', 'authority' in commentary). 22:22 'the key of the house of David', singular. 22:18, 23, 24 kāḇôḏ in non-divine constructs = 'glory' (wave ruling 2, strict; book-wide entry kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah): 'the chariots of your glory', 'a throne of glory', 'all the glory of his father's house'. 22:24 'the offspring and the issue'; ʾaggānôṯ 'cups', nᵉḇālîm 'flagons' (nēḇel II, distinct from nēḇel I 'harp' at 5:12; 14:11); the repeated kᵉlê kept with JPS 1917. 22:25 hammaśśāʾ (maśśāʾ I 'load') 'the burden' (ASV, JPS 1917), not governed by massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah.
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Hebrew is rare, elliptical or ambiguous. The line keeps a standard public-domain rendering, usually ASV and often shared by JPS 1917, and the commentary reports the alternatives; two items depart from ASV (22:5 and, by founder ruling 2026-11-26, 22:15). (a) 22:5: after yôm, the preposition lᵉ with the divine name is the possessive construction of 2:12 (kî yôm laYHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ), which the stable chapter prints as 'there is a day of YHWH of hosts'. ASV and JPS 1917 render lᵉ as 'from', a sense the preposition rarely has. NJPS reads possession ('my Lord GOD of Hosts had a day'), and NRSV is recalled as doing the same, not verified. The line therefore reads 'For the Lord YHWH of hosts has a day of …', which keeps the two verses concordant and adds nothing to the Hebrew. (b) kāḇôḏ at 22:18, 23, 24 refers to human status and possessions. Wave ruling 2 makes 'glory' strict for kāḇôḏ in every use, as the stable 10:3, 10:18 and 11:10 already show. ASV and JPS 1917 print 'glory' at 22:18 and 22:24 and ASV at 22:23, so the rule costs nothing against the baseline. The departures of JPS 1917 ('throne of honour') and NJPS ('seat of honor', 'substance', 'chariots bearing your body') are reported. 1 Sam 2:8 has the same kissēʾ kāḇôḏ, rendered 'the throne of glory' by ASV. (c) 22:6: ʾāḏām qualifies chariotry and refers to the crews of an army. Wave ruling 13 limits the gender-neutral rule of adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah to generic human nouns, so 'men' is kept. The remaining items follow ASV where the Hebrew admits it. At 22:3 both the agentive and the privative min are attested, and NJPS marks the line as uncertain. At 22:4 baṯ-ʿammî is the appositional genitive of baṯ-ṣiyyôn (1:8); the literal form keeps the personification, and NJPS gives the same sense in its note ('the young woman, my people'). The phrase is frequent in Jeremiah and Lamentations, and promotion to the central glossary is recommended when those books are drafted. At 22:5 the Kir / Shoa reading of JPS 1917 and NJPS is a recognised alternative (NJPS: 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'); MT's singular nouns are kept against ASV's plurals. At 22:15 sōḵēn occurs only here as an office title. Its Ugaritic and Phoenician cognates (skn, 'prefect') favour JPS 1917 / NJPS 'steward' (HALOT; recalled, not verified), and the line follows them with 'steward' (founder ruling 2026-11-26, on the Reviewer's recommendation; the Editor had proposed keeping ASV). ASV 'treasurer' names a fiscal office the Hebrew does not state and probably descends from the LXX ταμίας (recalled, not verified); it is reported in commentary. At 22:16, 19 the changes of person are MT's. The line keeps the third person at 22:16 with ASV alone (JPS 1917 'Thou that hewest thee out a sepulchre on high' and NJPS 'O you who have hewn your tomb on high' both convert to the second person) and follows all three references in rendering the indefinite third person of 22:19 as a passive, an ordinary English rendering of an impersonal subject. At 22:17-18 ASV's bracketed supplements ('[strong]', '[and toss thee]') are dropped or absorbed. The words are rare (ṭalṭēlāh; ṣᵉnēp̄āh; ʿṭh, possibly ʿṭh II 'grasp'), and the alternatives are reported. At 22:21 'girdle' and 'government' are kept with ASV, although the stable chapters use 'girdle' for ʾēzôr (11:5) and ḥăḡôrāh (3:24) and 'government' for miśrāh (9:5). The collisions are stated in commentary instead of being removed by a new gloss. At 22:24 ṣᵉp̄iʿôṯ occurs only here, and ASV's 'issue' is kept. At 22:25 the noun is maśśāʾ I 'load', not the heading noun maśśāʾ II of 22:1, and 'burden' is the ordinary English. The entry is direct, because every rendering is attested in ASV, JPS 1917 or NJPS and no reading is added.

entries.lemma: yāṯēḏ 'peg, pin, stake' (tent peg; wall peg; digging tool, Deut 23:14)
entries.literal: a peg driven in
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'nail' (Isa 22:23, 25; Ezra 9:8), 'stakes' (Isa 54:2), 'pin' (Judg 4:21; Ezek 15:3); JPS 1917 and NJPS 'peg' (Isa 22:23, 25)
entries.wohChoice: 'peg' where the yāṯēḏ is driven in to hold or carry a weight (22:23, 25: 'I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place'; 'the peg that was fastened in a sure place'). Context clause: 'stake(s)' for the pegs of a tent (54:2 'strengthen your stakes', stable, already so printed; 33:20 when drafted). Never 'nail', which in modern English denotes a metal fastener.
entries.rationale: A yāṯēḏ is a pointed wooden or metal peg. It is driven into the ground to hold a tent (Judg 4:21; Exod 27:19), into a wall to hang things on (Ezek 15:3, 'a pin to hang any vessel thereon', ASV), or carried as a digging tool (Deut 23:14) (BDB; HALOT). In Isa 22:23-25 the image is a peg driven (tqʿ) into a firm place, on which the household's vessels are hung (22:24). JPS 1917 and NJPS render it 'peg', and so does this entry. ASV's 'nail' reflects older English usage, but a modern reader takes it for a metal nail hammered flat. The stable 54:2 prints the tent sense as 'stakes', the normal English for tent pegs, and the entry keeps that wording as a context clause instead of changing a stable line. One Hebrew word therefore has two English renderings divided by context, and both are standard glosses. The entry is direct because both renderings are the ordinary lexical senses attested in the public-domain versions. Orchestrator: ISA-54:2 is in a stable chapter, so its glossaryRefs need the new id when the diff is merged; its English line is unchanged. Wave I-5 (Isa 33): tent context clause applied at 33:20, 'whose stakes shall never be pulled up' (ASV and JPS 1917 'stakes'; NJPS 'pegs'; checked 2026-11-26).
