entries.wohChoice: 23:1 privative 'so that there is no house, no entering in' (ASV, JPS 1917); NJPS construal and the harbor sense in commentary. Place names: 'Tarshish', 'ships of Tarshish' (as 2:16; wave I-4 ruling 8), 'Kittim' (23:1, 12, qere), 'Shihor' without the article (MT, JPS 1917, NJPS; against ASV 'the Shihor'), 'Canaan' (23:11), 'Chaldeans' (23:13, as 13:19; 43:14; 48:14, 20; central eretz-kasdim not applied); identifications (Cyprus, a Nile branch, Phoenicia, Babylonia) in commentary only. 23:2 MT 'Be still … you whom the merchants of Sidon, crossing the sea, have filled' (ASV); NJPS 'Moan' and the 1QIsaᵃ mlʾkyk 'your messengers' in commentary. 23:3 'the market of nations'. 23:4 and 23:12 bᵉṯûlāh 'virgin(s)' (ASV, JPS 1917). 23:5 temporal 'When the report comes to Egypt' (ASV). 23:7 'jubilant city' ('city' supplied) and 23:12 'exult' for the root ʿlz, kept apart from śmḥ 'rejoice'. 23:8 'the bestower of crowns' (ASV); kinʿāneyhā 'traders'; niḵbaddê-ʾāreṣ 'the honored of the earth' (23:8, 9; as 43:4 'you are honored'). 23:9 lᵉḥallēl 'to profane', lᵉhāqēl 'to bring into contempt' (the qll/kbd wordplay in commentary). 23:10 MT and ASV 'there is no restraint any more'; NJPS 'harbor', the LXX 'work your land … ships no longer come from Carthage' (Rahlfs) and the 'ships of Tarshish' emendation (partial LXX support) in commentary. 23:11 māʿuzneyhā 'its strongholds'. 23:13 MT and ASV in the line, 'Behold, the land of the Chaldeans! This people was not; Assyria founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up his siege towers, they overthrew its palaces; he made it a ruin' (qere, MT number kept); repunctuation, kittîm emendation, 'ships' and gloss theories in commentary. 23:15 'like the days of one king'. 23:16 kinnôr 'lyre' (as 5:12; 24:8), 'play skillfully'. 23:17 pqd 'visit' (ASV) for the restoration sense. 23:18 'holiness to YHWH' (ASV, JPS 1917), 'durable clothing' (ASV) with 'stately / fine' in commentary.
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator asked the Editor to choose between standard renderings. The Editor keeps the Masoretic Text and the public-domain baseline (ASV, checked with JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 on Sefaria) unless the book's concordance requires a change. Every alternative is recorded in commentary, no item adopts an emendation, and no item carries a project reading. The place names follow wave I-4 ruling 4, with ASV spellings for names that no entry fixes. The one exception is Shihor: MT has no article, and JPS 1917 and NJPS omit it. The ʿlz and kbd choices keep the root concordance of the book (32:13 'the jubilant city'; 43:4 'you are honored'). The Niphal participle niḵbaddê is a verbal form, not the noun kāḇôḏ, so the strict 'glory' rule of wave I-4 ruling 2 does not apply to it. At 23:13 all three PD references and NRSV construe the verse differently, and NJPS marks it 'Meaning of verse uncertain'. The line therefore follows MT with ASV's wording and keeps MT's shift of number, which ASV smooths, while the commentary gives the repunctuation, the kittîm emendation (NJPS note), the 'ships' reading of ṣiyyîm (JPS 1917, NJPS) and the gloss hypothesis. Two of the Translator's attributions were corrected after checking. 'Remember' at 23:17 is JPS 1917; NJPS reads 'take note of'. At 23:10 the reported 1QIsaᵃ reading 'ships of Tarshish' is not supported by the online collation of col. XVIII by Fred P. Miller (ao.net/~fmoeller), which lists no variant there. The scroll readings cited (23:2 mlʾkyk; 23:11, 13, 15) come from that collation and were not checked against DJD 32. pqd 'visit' at 23:17 is deliberately kept apart from the judgment rendering 'punished' of yippaqedu-pqd-visitation-imprisonment-isaiah-24, because here the visitation restores Tyre. All choices are standard renderings, so the claim is direct.

entries.partOfSpeech: noun (feminine), absolute and construct, with and without suffixes
entries.literal: adornment, beauty; that in which one glories or takes pride
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'the beauty of their anklets' (3:18), 'excellent and comely' (4:2, adjectival), 'the glory of his high looks' (10:12), 'the beauty of the Chaldeans' pride' (13:19), 'their glory' (20:5), 'according to the beauty of a man' (44:13); JPS 1917 'the bravery of their anklets' (3:18), 'the glory of his haughty looks' (10:12), 'the beauty of the Chaldeans' pride' (13:19), 'their glory' (20:5), 'according to the beauty of a man' (44:13); NJPS 'the finery' (3:18), 'majestic pride' (10:12), 'Proud splendor of the Chaldeans' (13:19), 'their boast' (20:5), 'The beauty of a man' (44:13) (Sefaria, checked 2026-11-26)
entries.wohChoice: 'honor' is the book default for tip̄ʾereṯ (wave I-4 ruling 2; founder ruling 2026-11-26): 4:2 'pride and honor'; 20:5 'Egypt their honor'. The default keeps 'glory' for kāḇôḏ (kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah), 'splendor' for hāḏār (hadar-splendor-isaiah), 'beauty' for ṣᵉḇî (tsevi-beauty-isaiah) and 'majesty' for gāʾôn. Recorded departures, where the idiom does not allow 'honor': 3:18 'the finery of the anklets' (ornament; daughters-of-zion-finery-isaiah-3); 10:12 'the boasting of his haughty looks' (pejorative, tied to the Hithpael 'boast itself' of 10:15; lexical-cruxes-isaiah-10); 13:19 'the splendor of the pride of the Chaldeans' (Babylon as the Chaldeans' ornament; NJPS 'Proud splendor'; 'beauty' is taken by ṣᵉḇî in the same verse); 44:13 'with the beauty of a human being' (the physical form of the idol; ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS 'beauty'). The stable departures are recorded, not reopened. Future sites take 'honor' unless their Editor records a departure here.
entries.rationale: tip̄ʾereṯ is the ornament or beauty in which someone takes pride, and so also that pride itself, honour or boasting (BDB; HALOT; recalled). The English versions render it by context, 'beauty', 'glory', 'bravery', 'finery', 'boast' and 'splendor', and ASV's commonest choice, 'glory', would merge it with kāḇôḏ, which wave I-4 ruling 2 keeps strict. 'Honor' is the sense of the word in the triad 'for praise, for fame and for honor' (Deut 26:19; Jer 13:11), and the stable 4:2 and the wave I-4 20:5 already print it. At 20:5 the noun is what the people boasted in, Egypt as the power they relied on (NJPS 'their boast'), and 'their honor' gives that sense without 'glory'. Where 'honor' would invert or obscure the sense, the book has departed and the departures are listed in wohChoice so that a reader can audit them: an item of jewellery (3:18), the Assyrian king's arrogance (10:12), Babylon as ornament (13:19, where 'beauty' now renders ṣᵉḇî after the founder's ruling) and the beauty of the human form (44:13, which shares 'beauty' with ṣᵉḇî as a recorded collision). The entry was created at the wave I-4 sign-off (founder ruling 2026-11-26), as the chapter 20 Editor and Reviewer recommended, to take the tip̄ʾereṯ item out of the verse-scoped tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4. The renderings are standard glosses and carry no lens, so the claim is direct. Wave I-5: 28:1, 4 'the beauty of its honor'; 28:5 liṣp̄îraṯ tip̄ʾārāh 'a diadem of honor' (NJPS 'a diadem of glory'; ASV 'a diadem of beauty'). The default holds; no departure recorded.

entries.source: כָּבוֹד (of persons, peoples and their possessions)
entries.strongs: H3519 (kāḇôḏ 'weight, abundance, honour, glory'); cf. H3513 (kāḇēḏ 'be heavy, be honoured'). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: kāḇôḏ 'weight; wealth, abundance; dignity, honour; glory', here of human beings, nations, cities and their goods
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (masculine), absolute and construct, with and without suffixes
entries.literal: weight, heaviness; hence substance, dignity, glory
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'glory' at 8:7; 10:3, 16, 18; 14:18; 16:14; 17:3, 4; 21:16; 22:18, 23, 24, 'glorious' at 4:2 and 11:10, and 'their honorable men' at 5:13; JPS 1917 'glory' at most of these sites, 'their honourable men' (5:13), 'a throne of honour' (22:23); NJPS by context: 'all his multitude' (8:7), 'your carcasses' (10:3), 'its body' (10:16), 'the mass' (10:18; 17:4), 'shall be honored' (11:10), 'in honor' (14:18), 'Moab's population' (16:14), 'the mass of Israelites' (17:3), 'all the multitude of Kedar' (21:16), 'chariots bearing your body' (22:18), 'a seat of honor' (22:23), 'all the substance' (22:24) (Sefaria, checked 2026-11-26)
entries.wohChoice: 'glory' for the noun kāḇôḏ also where it is the glory of persons, peoples and their possessions (wave I-4 ruling 2: 'glory' for kāḇôḏ is strict; founder ruling 2026-11-26): 4:2 'beauty and glory' (predicated of the growth of the land); 8:7 'the king of Assyria and all his glory'; 10:3 'where will you leave your glory?'; 10:16 'under his glory'; 10:18 'the glory of his forest'; 11:10 'his resting place shall be glory'; 14:18 'lie in glory'; 16:14 'the glory of Moab'; 17:3 'the glory of the children of Israel'; 17:4 'the glory of Jacob'; 21:16 'all the glory of Kedar'; 22:18 'the chariots of your glory'; 22:23 'a throne of glory'; 22:24 'all the glory of his father's house'. The senses of wealth, multitude, body and rank are given in commentary, not in the line, and the noun is kept where ASV turns it into an adjective (4:2; 11:10 'glorious'). One recorded departure: 5:13 kᵉḇôḏô 'their honored men' (stable; ASV, JPS 1917), where the noun is a collective for the nobility set against hămônô 'its multitude'. Outside this entry: the divine kāḇôḏ (central kavod-yhwh; overlay kevodo-kavod-suffixed-isaiah, kavod-labanah-chammah-isaiah-24); 4:5 'over all the glory', whose referent (Zion's glory or the divine presence) is disputed; and the verb and participles of kbd ('honor', 'the honored', 23:8-9).
entries.rationale: kāḇôḏ comes from kbd 'be heavy', and of human beings it is their weight in the world: wealth (Gen 31:1), multitude, rank and splendour (BDB; HALOT; recalled). NJPS renders it by that contextual sense ('multitude', 'mass', 'body', 'substance', 'honor'), which interprets each site, while ASV and JPS 1917 print 'glory' at nearly every one of them. Wave I-4 ruling 2 makes 'glory' strict for kāḇôḏ so that one Hebrew noun keeps one English word across the book, and the stable chapters already apply it at 8:7, 10:3, 10:16, 10:18, 11:10 and 14:18. One English word also lets the reader see that the book uses the same noun for the glory of Assyria, Moab, Kedar, Jacob and Shebna (10:16-18; 16:14; 17:3-4; 21:16; 22:18) and for the glory of YHWH (6:3; 40:5). The one departure, 5:13 'their honored men', is ASV's and JPS 1917's rendering of a collective that names persons, where 'their glory are famished' is not English; it is recorded so that the concordance can be audited. The entry was created at the wave I-4 sign-off (founder ruling 2026-11-26) to gather the non-divine sites that earlier sat only in chapter-scoped entries (lexical-cruxes-isaiah-10, lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22). The rendering is the standard English of the PD versions and carries no lens, so the claim is direct. Wave I-5 (Isa 35): 35:2 kᵉḇôḏ hallᵉḇānôn 'the glory of Lebanon shall be given to it' (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS 'glory', checked 2026-11-26). The glory of a region given to the desert stands in the same verse as kᵉḇôḏ-YHWH (central kavod-yhwh), so one English word lets the reader see the repetition of the noun.

entries.strongs: H6643 (ṣᵉḇî; the entry covers ṣᵉḇî I 'beauty, ornament, splendour', not the homonym ṣᵉḇî II 'gazelle'). Strong's number from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: ṣᵉḇî I 'beauty, ornament, splendour'
entries.literal: ornament, beauty, a thing of splendour
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'beautiful' (4:2, adjectival), 'the glory of kingdoms' (13:19), 'the pride of all glory' (23:9), 'Glory to the righteous' (24:16); JPS 1917 'beautiful' (4:2), 'the glory of kingdoms' (13:19), 'the pride of all glory' (23:9), 'Glory to the righteous' (24:16); NJPS 'beauty' (4:2), 'glory of kingdoms' (13:19), 'all glorious beauty' (23:9), 'Glory to the righteous!' (24:16) (Sefaria, checked 2026-11-26)
entries.wohChoice: 'beauty' is the book default for ṣᵉḇî I, so that 'glory' stays reserved for kāḇôḏ (wave I-4 ruling 2; founder ruling 2026-11-26): 4:2 'beauty and glory'; 13:19 'Babylon, the beauty of kingdoms' (stable line revised 2026-11-26, chapter 13 version 1.0.1); 23:9 'to profane the pride of all beauty'. Recorded idiomatic departure: 24:16 ṣᵉḇî laṣṣaddîq 'Glory to the righteous one!' (stable; ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS 'Glory'), where the noun is the content of an acclamation and 'Beauty to the righteous one!' would not be English. The homonym ṣᵉḇî II 'gazelle' (13:14 'like a hunted gazelle') is outside the entry. Future sites (28:1, 4, 5 and later) take 'beauty' unless their Editor records a departure here.
entries.rationale: ṣᵉḇî I is 'beauty, ornament, splendour' (BDB; HALOT; recalled), the land or city as a jewel (Ezek 20:6, 15; Dan 11:16 'the beautiful land'). ASV and JPS 1917 often render it 'glory', which in this book would merge it with kāḇôḏ, and the stable 4:2 already prints ṣᵉḇî 'beauty' beside kāḇôḏ 'glory' in the same verse. The chapter 23 Editor extended that choice to 23:9 ('the pride of all beauty'; NJPS 'all glorious beauty') and reported that the stable 13:19 and 24:16 printed 'glory'. The founder ruled on 2026-11-26 (wave I-4 sign-off, decision 8) to revise 13:19 to 'the beauty of kingdoms', a phrase where 'beauty' reads naturally and keeps Babylon's description in the ornament register of the verse, and to keep 24:16 'Glory to the righteous one!' as a recorded departure, because in an acclamation English uses 'Glory to …' and the line would otherwise become unidiomatic. The entry takes over the ṣᵉḇî item from the verse-scoped tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4, which keeps the ṣemaḥ decision. The renderings are standard glosses and carry no lens, so the claim is direct. Wave I-5: 28:1, 4 ṣᵉḇî tip̄ʾartô 'the beauty of its honor' (literal construct; ASV, JPS 1917 'his glorious beauty' would need 'glory'); 28:5 ʿăṭereṯ ṣᵉḇî 'a crown of beauty' (NJPS 'a crown of beauty'; ASV and JPS 1917 assign 'beauty' to the other noun). No departure recorded. Wave I-5 (Isa 33): 'beauty' is also the book's English for yōp̄î (33:17 'the king in his beauty'; stable 3:24 'branding instead of beauty'), recorded in overlay yofi-beauty-isaiah. The two nouns never share an Isaiah verse, so the overlap hides no contrast; an Editor who meets both in one verse must separate them.

entries.strongs: H3933 (laʿaḡ 'mocking; stammering'); H3932 (lāʿaḡ 'mock', Niphal 'stammer'); H3934 (lāʿēḡ). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: lʿg: laʿaḡ 'mocking, derision; (barbarous) stammering' (pl. cstr. laʿăḡê, 28:11; some lexica refer the form to the adjective lāʿēḡ); Niphal participle nilʿaḡ 'stammering' (33:19)
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (plural construct) with śāp̄āh 'lip' (28:11); Niphal participle with lāšôn 'tongue' (33:19)
entries.literal: with stammerings of lip (28:11); stammering of tongue (33:19)
entries.standardEnglish: 28:11: ASV 'by men of strange lips'; KJV, JPS 1917, Koren 'with stammering lips'; NJPS 'in a stammering jargon'; LXX διὰ φαυλισμὸν χειλέων 'through contempt of lips'; 1 Cor 14:21 (ASV) 'by men of strange tongues and by the lips of strangers'. 33:19: JPS 1917 'of a stammering tongue' (per wave I-5 rule 7; to be re-checked by the chapter 33 Editor)
entries.wohChoice: One English root for lʿg as the speech of foreigners: 28:11 kî bᵉlaʿăḡê śāp̄āh ûḇᵉlāšôn ʾaḥereṯ 'For with stammering lips and with another tongue'; 33:19 nilʿaḡ lāšôn, 'stammering' (wording of the whole phrase left to the chapter 33 Editor, who appends ISA-33:19). ASV's supplied 'men of' is not printed. The 'mocking' sense of the root (28:14, 22 use the different root lṣ for 'scoff') is given in commentary, not in the line. Other occurrences of lʿg meaning 'mock, deride' (e.g. 37:22 lāʿăḡāh lāḵ 'she has mocked you', when drafted) are outside this entry and take 'mock'.
entries.rationale: BDB s.v. laʿaḡ gives two senses, 'mocking, derision' and '(barbarous) stammering', and lists ל׳ שָׂפָה Isa 28:11 under the second, parallel to lāšôn ʾaḥereṯ 'another tongue'. The same article records Gesenius, Delitzsch, Cheyne and Duhm referring the form to the adjective lāʿēḡ, and Graetz's emendation to the root ʿlg (BDB checked via Sefaria's lexicon, 2026-11-26). For 33:19 BDB gives the Niphal participle as 'a people stammering of tongue (i.e. barbarians)', with cognates in Syriac and Targumic Aramaic meaning 'stutter'. The two Isaiah passages describe the same thing, the unintelligible language of a foreign invader, and so the entry gives them one English root, as wave I-5 rule 7 rules. 'Stammering' is the reading of KJV, JPS 1917, Koren and NJPS at 28:11 (all checked 2026-11-26); ASV's 'strange lips' renders the sense but supplies 'men of' and loses the sound-word, which 28:10, 13 make prominent. The choice is the lexical sense and the majority English rendering, so the claim is direct. The play on the scoffers' own mocking is real in the Hebrew but belongs to commentary, since 'mocking lips' would lose the contrast with 'another tongue'. Paul's free quotation at 1 Cor 14:21 is reception, noted in commentary only. Wave I-5 (Isa 33): nilʿaḡ lāšôn at 33:19 is 'of a stammering tongue', the same English root as laʿăḡê śāp̄āh 'stammering lips' at 28:11 (ruling 7). JPS 1917 'Of a stammering tongue' and NJPS 'So stammering of tongue' have the same word; ASV has 'of a strange tongue' (all checked 2026-11-26). The Translator's 'strange' is replaced. The id matches the chapter-28 add in wave-i5-ch28-overlay-diff.json (confirmed at review); apply that add first.

entries.translit: hinᵉnî yissaḏ bᵉṣiyyôn ʾāḇen ʾeḇen bōḥan pinnaṯ yiqraṯ mûsāḏ mûssāḏ hammaʾămîn lōʾ yāḥîš
entries.strongs: H3245 (yāsaḏ); H68 (ʾeḇen); H976 (bōḥan); H6438 (pinnāh); H3368 (yāqār); H4143 (mûsāḏ); H539 (ʾmn Hiphil); H2363 (ḥûš). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: yāsaḏ 'found' (Piel); ʾeḇen bōḥan 'tested stone'; pinnaṯ yiqraṯ 'precious cornerstone'; mûsāḏ mûssāḏ 'a foundation founded'; ḥûš 'make haste'
entries.partOfSpeech: verbal clause (hinᵉnî + Piel perfect 3ms) with appositional noun phrases; Hiphil participle + negated Qal imperfect
entries.literal: behold me, (he) has founded in Zion a stone, a stone of testing, a corner of preciousness, a foundation founded; the one who trusts will not hurry
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner-stone of sure foundation: he that believeth shall not be in haste'; JPS 1917 '… a costly corner-stone of sure foundation; He that believeth shall not make haste'; NJPS 'Behold, I will found in Zion, Stone by stone, A tower of precious cornerstones, Exceedingly firm; He who trusts need not fear' ('Meaning of Heb. uncertain'); LXX 'the one who believes in him will not be put to shame' (οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ), quoted at Rom 9:33; 10:11; 1 Pet 2:6
entries.wohChoice: 28:16 'Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone of sure foundation; the one who believes will not be in haste.' MT is translated: ASV's present 'I lay' renders hinᵉnî yissaḏ (the 3ms perfect pointing and the participle proposal are reported in commentary); bōḥan 'tested' (BDB) for ASV 'tried'; yāḥîš 'will not be in haste' (ḥûš 'make haste', BDB), not the LXX 'will not be put to shame'. The New Testament reception (Rom 9:33, joined to 8:14; Rom 10:11; 1 Pet 2:6, joined to Ps 118:22; Eph 2:20) is reported in commentary only (wave I-5 rule 2). Neither the line nor the entry identifies the stone.
entries.rationale: The verse is one of the most quoted in Isaiah, and the wave rulings bind its handling in advance: NT reception in commentary only. MT points yissaḏ as a Piel perfect third person after the first-person hinᵉnî. BDB (s.v. yāsaḏ) records Cheyne's reading of the participle yōsēḏ, and the English versions all render a first-person present or future ('I lay', ASV, JPS 1917, Koren; 'I will found', NJPS; checked 2026-11-26). The line takes that consensus sense; the morphology is reported. BDB s.v. bōḥan glosses ʾeḇen bōḥan 'a tested, tried stone, i.e. approved for use as a foundation-stone' (checked via Sefaria's lexicon), so 'tested' is the lexical rendering and avoids the archaic 'tried'. BDB s.v. ḥûš gives 'haste, make haste'; ASV's 'shall not be in haste' is exact, and NJPS 'need not fear' paraphrases the sense (panic flight). The LXX 'shall not be put to shame' (getbible.net LXX, checked) reflects a different reading or interpretation and reached the NT through Paul and 1 Peter (ASV NT checked). Translating MT and reporting the LXX and its reception follows mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah. The rendering is the standard one, so the claim is direct. The entry exists so that the stone verse has an auditable record: the line carries no Christological or other identification of the stone, and any lens reading is confined to a labelled speculative paragraph. Reviewer correction (2026-11-26): the source has the long form הִנְנִי, transliterated hinᵉnî.

entries.lemma: single-site lexical and syntactic decisions of Isaiah 28
entries.literal: see wohChoice
entries.standardEnglish: ASV, KJV (getbible.net), JPS 1917, NJPS 1985 and Koren (Sefaria) checked 2026-11-26 for every verse; readings given per item in the chapter commentary
entries.wohChoice: 28:1, 4 gêʾ-šᵉmānîm 'the rich valley' (Koren; ASV 'the fat valley'; NJPS's gēʾê 'men bloated with rich food' in commentary). 28:2 lāʾāreṣ 'to the ground' in the idiom of casting down, as the book prints 14:12; 21:9; 25:12; 26:5 (governed by no ʾereṣ entry; the draft's 'to the earth' changed); bᵉyāḏ 'with the hand' (ASV). 28:4 and 28:24-28: the generic participle is rendered neutrally ('the one who looks upon it'; 'the one who plows'), and the Hebrew 3ms pronouns resuming it are kept ('his hand … he swallows it'; 'his ground', 'his cart'), as ASV and NJPS; qayiṣ 'summer' (ASV). 28:7 ASV: 'they are swallowed up by wine' (blʿ 'swallow', echoing 28:4, not the 'confuse' homonym of JPS 1917 / NJPS); 'they err in vision, they stumble in judgment'. 28:8 'so that there is no place clean' (ASV). 28:9-10 no quotation marks (ASV; NJPS's attribution to the drunkards in commentary). 28:14 mōšᵉlê 'who rule' (mšl I, ASV; mšl II 'ballad-mongers' JPS 1917 / 'composers of taunt-verses' NJPS note in commentary); ʾanšê lāṣôn 'you scoffers'. 28:15, 18 māweṯ lower-case 'death' (as 25:8, billa-hamavet-death-swallowed-isaiah-25; NJPS 'Death' and the Mot comparison in commentary); ḥōzeh / ḥāzûṯ 'agreement' (ASV; BDB's 'vision' proposal in commentary). 28:18 wᵉḵuppar 'annulled' (kpr in its legal sense; kupar-atonement-isaiah deliberately not applied). 28:21 'Mount Perazim', 'the valley of Gibeon' (ASV); yirgāz 'he will rage' (BDB 'be agitated'; ASV 'be wroth'; NJPS 'rouse Himself'); appositive syntax with maʿăśeh 'deed' / ʿăḇōḏāh 'work' and zār 'strange' / nāḵrîyāh 'alien' distinguished. 28:25, 27 qeṣaḥ 'black cumin' (BDB Nigella sativa; JPS 1917, NJPS), replacing ASV's archaic and botanically wrong 'fitches' in the draft; śôrāh 'in rows' (ASV; BDB's dittography view in commentary); nisman 'in the appointed place' (no suffix; draft 'its' corrected); kussemeṯ 'spelt' (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS 'emmer' in commentary); gᵉḇulāṯô 'in its border'. 28:26 accent-based division 'For he instructs him aright; his God teaches him' (MT ṭip̄ḥā on lammišpāṭ, conjunctive mērᵊḵā on ʾĕlōhāyw; JPS 1917, NJPS, Koren), replacing the draft's ASV construal 'For his God instructs him aright; he teaches him' (the sense is unchanged, God being the subject of both verbs). 28:27 ḥārûṣ 'threshing sledge' (BDB adj. 'sharp' used as noun; homonym of the ḥārûṣ 'determined' of 10:22, central kalah-venecheratzah entry not applied); maṭṭeh 'staff', šēḇeṭ 'rod' (as 10:5). 28:28 dqq 'crush' at both sites; ASV construal 'for he will not go on threshing it forever … and though the wheel of his cart and his horses scatter it'. 28:29 ASV relative clause 'who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in sound wisdom'; tûšîyāh 'sound wisdom'; the 9:5 / 25:1 echo noted, pele-etzot-emunah-hymn-vocabulary-isaiah-25 not applied. Founder ruling (sign-off 2026-11-26) on pronouns resuming a generic participle: neutral noun, Hebrew pronoun. The generic participle takes a neutral noun phrase and the resuming 3ms pronouns stay 'he/his' (28:4; 28:24-28); singular 'they' was considered and rejected.
entries.rationale: Each item is a single-site decision with no lens content, collected in one entry as the book does for every chapter (compare lexical-cruxes-isaiah-18). Most items keep the Translator's ASV-based line and record the alternatives, so the auditor can see what was weighed. Three line changes are made by this entry. First, 28:2 'to the ground': the book already prints lāʾāreṣ in the idiom of throwing or falling down as 'to the ground' (stable 14:12; 21:9; 25:12; 26:5), and the central eretz rationale records that the idiom is governed by no ʾereṣ entry (wave I-4, at 21:9); NJPS has 'to the ground'. Second, 28:25, 27 'black cumin': BDB s.v. qeṣaḥ identifies the plant as Nigella sativa, with LXX μελάνθιον and Vulgate gith (checked via Sefaria's lexicon, 2026-11-26), and JPS 1917 and NJPS print 'black cummin / black cumin'; ASV's 'fitches' is an English plant-name for vetch, which misidentifies the crop for a modern reader. Third, 28:25 'the appointed place': nisman has no suffix. The pronoun practice at 28:4 and 28:24-28 extends wave I-4 rule 13 (generic nouns neutral) only as far as the noun: the resuming 3ms pronouns are kept, because the figures are single individuals in a simile and a parable and singular 'they' would obscure the Hebrew agreement; the founder confirmed this practice (sign-off 2026-11-26: neutral noun, Hebrew pronoun). The 28:18 kpr item records why the atonement rendering of kupar-atonement-isaiah is not used: the subject is a covenant, and every English version consulted has 'annulled / disannulled'. The 28:27 ḥārûṣ item records a homonym so that the central kalah-venecheratzah entry is not wrongly extended. Sources: BDB (Sefaria lexicon) for laʿaḡ, ṣaw, qaw, ḥārûṣ, ḥûš, yāsaḏ, bōḥan, ḥōzeh, ḥāzûṯ, rāḡaz, qeṣaḥ, śôrāh; ASV, KJV and LXX on getbible.net; JPS 1917, NJPS and Koren on Sefaria; all checked 2026-11-26. All renderings are standard, so the claim is direct. Post-review (2026-11-26): the 28:26 item follows the cantillation, on the Reviewer's revise verdict; the draft and the first Editor pass had followed ASV against the accents and against JPS 1917, NJPS and Koren. The pronoun item stands as option A by founder ruling (sign-off 2026-11-26: neutral noun, Hebrew pronoun); the singular-'they' alternative (option B) was rejected and is no longer staged.

entries.strongs: H1935 (hôḏ); H6963 (qôl). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: hôḏ 'splendour, majesty, vigour'
entries.literal: the splendour / majesty of his voice
entries.standardEnglish: ASV and JPS 1917 'his glorious voice'; NJPS 'His majestic voice' (all checked 2026-11-26: ASV via bible-api.com, JPS 1917 and NJPS via Sefaria API v3)
entries.wohChoice: 'grandeur' is the book-wide rendering of hôḏ in Isaiah (founder sign-off 2026-11-26): 30:30 'And YHWH will cause the grandeur of his voice to be heard'. The construct noun is kept and not turned into an adjective. The choice keeps each of the book's reserved words to its own noun: 'glory' for kāḇôḏ (kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah), 'splendor' for hāḏār (hadar-splendor-isaiah), 'majesty' for gāʾôn and gēʾûṯ of God (geut-majesty-isaiah), 'honor' for tip̄ʾereṯ (tiferet-honor-isaiah), 'beauty' for ṣᵉḇî (tsevi-beauty-isaiah). Alternative considered and not adopted by the founder: NJPS 'majesty' ('the majesty of his voice'), with the overlap with gāʾôn/gēʾûṯ recorded as a departure. ASV 'glorious' is not used, because 'glory/glorious' is reserved for kāḇôḏ.
entries.rationale: hôḏ is 'splendour, majesty, vigour' (BDB; HALOT; recalled), the visible weight of a king or of God (Ps 21:6; 45:4; 104:1), and also the authority Moses passes to Joshua (Num 27:20). It occurs in Isaiah only at 30:30 (not concordance-verified). Every standard English gloss for it is already reserved by this book for another noun: 'glory' strictly for kāḇôḏ (wave I-4 ruling 2), 'splendor' for hāḏār, 'majesty' for gāʾôn/gēʾûṯ of God, 'honor' for tip̄ʾereṯ and 'beauty' for ṣᵉḇî. ASV and JPS 1917 'his glorious voice' would put the kāḇôḏ word on hôḏ, and NJPS 'His majestic voice' would put the gāʾôn word on it. 'Grandeur' is a plain English synonym of 'majesty' in the lexical range of the noun, and it lets the frequent pair hôḏ wᵉhāḏār (Ps 96:6; 104:1; 111:3; Job 40:10; 1 Chr 16:27) read 'grandeur and splendor' if the pair occurs in a later Isaiah-governed text or if the entry is promoted. The corpus outside Isaiah is not settled and is not reopened here: psalms-woh Ps 8:2 prints hôḏ 'your splendor', job-woh Job 37:22 'fearsome majesty' and Job 40:10 'honor and splendor' (hôḏ wᵉhāḏār), daniel-woh Dan 11:21 'the honor of the kingdom'. A later central entry could unify them; for now the decision is Isaiah-only and goes to the overlay. The noun is kept in construct ('the grandeur of his voice'), as the book keeps kāḇôḏ as a noun where ASV makes it an adjective (kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah at 4:2, 11:10). The word is a lexical gloss chosen for concordance and carries no lens, so the claim is direct; because it departs from all three checked versions, it was put to the founder and accepted (sign-off 2026-11-26).

entries.lemma: the two 'seer' nouns of Isaiah and their verbs
entries.partOfSpeech: nouns (participles used as titles) and finite verbs
entries.literal: to the seers (ones who see) … and to the ones who see visions: 'Do not see' … 'Do not see visions for us of right things … see visions of deceptions'
entries.standardEnglish: ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS: 'to the seers … to the prophets', with the ḥzh verbs rendered 'prophesy' (all checked 2026-11-26)
entries.wohChoice: rōʾeh 'seer'; ḥōzeh 'seer' where it stands alone or beside nāḇîʾ (29:10, stable: 'the prophets … the seers'), and 'visionary' where rōʾeh stands beside it (30:10); the verb rʾh 'see'; the verb ḥzh 'see visions' only where it stands beside rʾh with these titles (30:10), and elsewhere 'see' / 'saw' as in the stable 1:1, 2:1, 13:1 ('which he saw') and 26:11 ('they do not see') and the wave I-5 33:17, 20. nāḇîʾ is always 'prophet', and 'prophesy' is kept for the verb nbʾ. 30:10: 'who say to the seers, “Do not see,” and to the visionaries, “Do not see for us visions of what is right; speak to us smooth things, see visions of deceptions;”'. Outside the entry: the noun rōʾeh 'vision' at 28:7 (chapter 28 Editor) and the participle rōʾîm 'those who see' at 32:3 (stable).
entries.rationale: Isa 30:10 sets two titles side by side, rōʾîm and ḥōzîm, both meaning 'one who sees' (BDB; HALOT 'seer, visionary'; recalled), and the verse contains no nāḇîʾ. The English versions print 'the seers … the prophets' and render the ḥzh verbs 'prophesy', which gives the reader a word the Hebrew does not use. In this book that matters: the stable 29:10 prints nᵉḇîʾîm 'the prophets' and ḥōzîm 'the seers', so the ASV wording at 30:10 would give 'the prophets' to two different nouns, and 'seers' to two different nouns, in neighbouring chapters. Keeping 'seer' for rōʾeh (the older title of 1 Sam 9:9) and using 'visionary' for ḥōzeh only where both stand together keeps 29:10 intact and keeps each root visible in 30:10; the verbs follow ('Do not see' / 'see visions') at this pairing only; elsewhere the book renders ḥzh plainly 'see' / 'saw' (post-review scope correction). 'Visionary' is a standard lexical gloss of ḥōzeh and carries no lens, so the claim is direct. The change departs from all three checked versions in the line, and it was reported to the founder with the ASV wording as the alternative and accepted (sign-off 2026-11-26).

entries.strongs: H7294 (Rahab, the monster; also a name for Egypt); H7293 (rahaḇ 'storm, arrogance'); H7674 (šeḇeṯ / šāḇeṯ). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: Rahab, the name of the sea monster, applied to Egypt
entries.partOfSpeech: proper noun; at 30:7 followed by the pronoun hēm and a noun or infinitive of šbt
entries.literal: Rahab, they (are) sitting-still / cessation
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'Rahab that sitteth still'; JPS 1917 'arrogancy that sitteth still'; NJPS 'They are a threat that has ceased' (note: meaning uncertain; emendation 'Disgrace and chagrin') (all checked 2026-11-26)
entries.wohChoice: 'Rahab' transliterated as the proper name of the sea monster in Isaiah: 30:7 'therefore I have called her Rahab who sits still' (MT; ASV), with hēm 'they' left unrendered as in ASV; the same name at 51:9 when that chapter is drafted. Not JPS 1917's common noun 'arrogancy', and not an emended text. The myth (Ps 89:11; Job 26:12; Ps 87:4 Rahab = Egypt) and the emendations are given in commentary only.
entries.rationale: Rahab is the name of the chaos monster subdued by YHWH (Isa 51:9; Ps 89:11 [Eng. 89:10]; Job 9:13; 26:12) and, at Ps 87:4, a poetic name for Egypt (BDB; HALOT; recalled), so a taunt that names Egypt 'Rahab' is lexically expected, and ASV and NRSV-type versions print the name. JPS 1917 reads the common noun rahaḇ 'arrogance' instead, and NJPS gives up the name and marks the line as uncertain. The line keeps MT and the name because the consonants and pointing are those of the name, and because 51:9 needs the same English word if the book's two Rahab sites are to be seen together. hēm šāḇeṯ is difficult (literally 'they, a sitting still'); ASV's 'who sits still' gives the sense without the pronoun, and the line follows it, recording the literal shape and the proposed redivisions in commentary. The cross-corpus chaoskampf cluster is documented centrally (chaoskampf-sea-conflict-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible, extended to ISA-30:7) and stays out of the line. A transliterated name carries no lens, so the claim is direct.

entries.literal: to pour a libation / weave a web; to take refuge in the stronghold; my mouth they did not ask; his princes; his messengers; Zoan; Hanes; oracle of the beasts of the Negeb; breath and emptiness; for a later day, for ever / as a witness; straight things; deceptions; in oppression and the devious; jar of potters; pool; in returning/sitting still and rest; a thousand … rebuke; like the pole; he will be high; happy/blessed; he will dwell; your teacher(s); be cornered/hidden; bread of distress and water of oppression; like a menstruant / sick; cast image; seasoned fodder; like the light of the seven days; the wound of its blow; the name of YHWH; heaviness of uprising; with a sieve of worthlessness; a bridle that misleads; the descent of his arm; shattering and downpour; be shattered; with the rod he will strike; passing of the staff of foundation; waving; Topheth; for the king / for Molech; he made deep, made wide its pyre
entries.standardEnglish: ASV throughout (checked via bible-api.com 2026-11-26): 'make a league', 'to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh', 'asked at my mouth', 'their princes … their ambassadors', 'Zoan … Hanes', 'The burden of the beasts of the South', 'helpeth in vain', 'for the time to come for ever and ever', 'right things … deceits', 'oppression and perverseness', 'potter's vessel', 'In returning and rest', 'One thousand [shall flee] at the threat of one … a beacon', 'be exalted', 'blessed', 'For the people shall dwell', 'thy teachers', 'the bread of adversity and the water of affliction', 'as an unclean thing', 'savory provender', 'as the light of seven days … the stroke of their wound', 'in thick rising smoke', 'the sieve of destruction', 'the lighting down of his arm … a blast, and tempest', 'with his rod will he smite [him]', 'every stroke of the appointed staff … brandishing', 'a Topheth … for the king'. JPS 1917 and NJPS (Sefaria API v3, checked 2026-11-26) as cited in the commentary.
entries.wohChoice: 30:1 'make a league' (nsk I, treaty libation; ASV), with NJPS 'weaving schemes' and JPS 1917 'form projects' in commentary. 30:2 'to take refuge in the stronghold of Pharaoh' (JPS 1917; ʿwz); 'have not asked of my mouth' (idiom kept). 30:4 'his princes … his messengers' (Hebrew suffix; JPS 1917); 'Zoan', 'Hanes' (ASV spellings; Tanis and Heracleopolis in commentary). 30:6 heading 'The oracle concerning the beasts of the South' (MT; emendation in commentary). 30:7 heḇel wārîq adverbial 'in vain and to no purpose'. 30:8 lāʿaḏ 'for ever' (MT; NJPS/Targum 'witness' in commentary); yôm ʾaḥărôn 'the time to come', not 'the last day'. 30:10 nᵉḵōḥôṯ 'what is right', mahăṯallôṯ 'deceptions'. 30:12 ʿōšeq 'oppression' (MT). 30:14 nēḇel yôṣᵉrîm 'a potters' jar'; gebeʾ 'the cistern'. 30:15 kōh ʾāmar 'thus says' (as v. 12 and every other kōh ʾāmar line in the book; ASV and JPS 1917 'thus said'); šûḇāh 'returning' (ASV), neither 'sitting still' nor 'repentance' in the line. 30:17 the verbless first colon kept elliptical; gᵉʿārāh 'rebuke'; tōren 'beacon' (ASV, JPS 1917). 30:18 yārûm 'he will be exalted'; ʾašrê 'blessed' (as stable 32:20). 30:19 yēšēḇ finite 'a people shall dwell' (MT; the vocative in commentary). 30:20 môreyḵā singular, lower case, 'your teacher' (twice); yikkānēp̄ 'be hidden'; 'the bread of adversity and the water of affliction' (construct, ASV). 30:22 kᵉmô dāwāh 'as an unclean thing' (ASV); massēḵaṯ singular 'molten image'; tizrēm 'cast away' (MT vocalization). 30:24 ḥāmîṣ 'seasoned'. 30:26 'like the light of the seven days' (article rendered; the checked readings are Ibn Ezra's combined light, Radak's week or Solomon's dedication, the Talmud's messianic days, and the 343 of Targum and Rashi, and none of them is the creation week); maḥaṣ makkāṯô 'the wound of its blow' (singular suffix). 30:27 šēm-YHWH 'the name of YHWH' (literal); maśśāʾāh 'rising smoke'. 30:28 'the sieve of destruction'; 'a bridle that leads astray'. 30:30 naḥaṯ 'descent'; nep̄eṣ 'cloudburst', zerem 'tempest'. 30:31 yēḥaṯ 'be dismayed'; baššēḇeṭ yakkeh 'with the rod he will strike' (subject unmarked). 30:32 'every passing of the appointed staff'; tᵉnûp̄āh 'brandishing'. 30:33 tāp̄teh 'a Topheth' (ASV); lammeleḵ 'for the king' (MT pointing; NJPS 'Melech' / Molech in commentary); ASV's clause division 'he has made it deep and wide; its pyre is fire and wood in abundance'.
entries.rationale: Each item is a single-site decision that keeps a standard rendering of the Masoretic Text, chosen from ASV, JPS 1917 or NJPS (all checked), with the rejected options and emendations reported in the verse commentary; none of the choices carries the project's lens. Two items change the Translator's draft. At 30:20 the plural 'your teachers' (ASV) becomes the singular 'your teacher', because the verb yikkānēp̄ is singular and the yod-before-suffix form occurs with singular III-he nouns, as miqneyḵā 'your livestock' with a singular verb in 30:23 shows (GKC §93ss, recalled, not verified); JPS 1917 and NJPS read the singular, and Rashi (checked) identifies the teacher as God. The line keeps lower case so that the identification stays in the commentary, consistent with the book's lower-case divine epithets (yah-tzur-olamim-everlasting-rock-isaiah-26). The central elon-moreh entry cites Isa 30:20 for the common noun môreh, but its wohChoice governs the toponym of Gen 12:6, so it is not extended. At 30:26 the line renders the article of šiḇʿaṯ hayyāmîm with JPS 1917 and NJPS and no more; Targum Jonathan and Rashi read a multiplier of 343, Ibn Ezra the seven days' light combined, Radak the week's days combined or Solomon's dedication, b. Pesachim 68a and b. Sanhedrin 91b the days of the Messiah (checked by Editor and Reviewer), and none reads the creation week. At 30:15 the messenger formula kōh ʾāmar takes 'thus says', the book's rendering everywhere else (post-review concordance fix; ASV and JPS 1917 'thus said'). At 30:33 MT's lammeleḵ 'for the king' is kept against NJPS 'Melech', and JPS 1917's common noun 'a hearth' is not adopted, because the name tāp̄teh (a form of tōp̄eṯ) is the point of the oracle. The remaining items follow ASV wording where it is accurate, and modern English where ASV is archaic ('seasoned fodder' for 'savory provender', 'deceptions' for 'deceits'). The renderings are standard glosses, so the claim is direct.

entries.lemma: single-site lexical and syntactic decisions of Isaiah 31 not covered by a dedicated entry
entries.partOfSpeech: mixed (nouns, finite verbs, infinitives absolute, participles, prepositional phrases)
entries.literal: horsemen / horses; and he brought evil; the help of the workers of iniquity; he growls; the fullness of shepherds; he does not bow down; to wage war on/against Mount Zion; like birds flying; shielding and rescuing, passing over and delivering; turn to the one against whom they made the revolt deep, children of Israel; they will reject; sin (adverbial); and he will flee for himself; for forced labor; and his rock will pass away from terror; fire; furnace / oven
entries.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; alternatives from JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 (checked on Sefaria 2026-11-26) recorded in commentary
entries.wohChoice: 31:1 pārāšîm 'horsemen' (ASV, JPS 1917; as at 21:7; 22:6-7). 31:2 wayyāḇēʾ rāʿ 'and will bring evil' (ASV future; JPS 1917 present and NJPS past in commentary); rāʿ 'evil', not the 45:7 'calamity'; ʿezraṯ 'the help' (NJPS 'allies' in commentary). 31:4 liṣbōʾ ʿal-har-ṣiyyôn 'to fight upon Mount Zion and upon its hill' (ASV, JPS 1917), keeping the spatial sense of ʿal and leaving open the hostile reading of NJPS 'make war against' and of the stable 29:7-8 'fight against'; yehgeh 'growls'; mᵉlōʾ rōʿîm 'a multitude of shepherds'; lōʾ yaʿăneh 'nor does he abase himself'. 31:5 'Like birds hovering'; 'he will protect and deliver it, he will pass over and preserve it' (ASV, 'it' supplied); the Passover echo of psḥ (Exod 12:13, 23, 27) in commentary only. 31:6 'Turn, O children of Israel, to him from whom they have deeply revolted': MT's third person kept with NJPS, vocative moved forward (changed from the draft's ASV harmonisation 'you have deeply revolted'). 31:7 yimʾāsûn 'shall reject' (NJPS; concordant with 5:24 'rejected'; changed from the draft's 'cast away', which the book keeps for hišlîḵ at 2:20); ḥēṭʾ 'as a sin'. 31:8 'Assyria … him' (as 10:5, 24); wᵉnās lô 'he shall flee' (nws; NJPS nss 'shrivel' in commentary); lāmas 'forced labor'. 31:9 'his rock shall pass away by reason of terror' (ASV, JPS 1917; changed from the draft's 'for terror'); ʾûr 'fire'; tannûr 'furnace'.
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Hebrew is ambiguous or rare. The line keeps a standard public-domain rendering, usually ASV and often shared by JPS 1917, and the commentary reports the alternatives; three items change the Translator's draft. (a) 31:4 is the main crux. The verb ṣbʾ with ʿal means 'wage war against' (29:7-8, the same phrase ʿal-har ṣiyyôn; Num 31:7; Zech 14:12), and NJPS reads 'will descend to make war / Against the mount and the hill of Zion', so that the lion is YHWH and Zion his prey. ASV and JPS 1917 read 'to fight upon mount Zion', which allows a defensive battle and agrees with the protection of v. 5; the same verse uses ʿal spatially ('over his prey'). The line keeps 'upon', the basic spatial sense of the preposition, because it renders the Hebrew without settling a question the commentators still debate; 'against' would settle it one way and 'for' the other, and 'for' has no lexical support. The concordance with 29:8 is stated in the commentary. (b) 31:6 shifts from an imperative to a third-person verb. ASV and JPS 1917 bring the clause into the second person; NJPS keeps the third person with a vocative (checked). The line follows NJPS, because the change of person is MT's and an English reader can follow it once the vocative stands first; the subject analysis of bᵉnê yiśrāʾēl and NJPS's recorded emendation are reported. (c) 31:7 yimʾāsûn is from mʾs 'reject' (BDB; HALOT), which the book prints as 'rejected' at 5:24 and NJPS renders 'reject' here. ASV's 'cast away' copies 2:20, where the verb is hišlîḵ 'throw', so the draft gave two verbs one English word. (d) 31:9 'by reason of terror' restores the ASV and JPS 1917 wording for causal min; the draft's 'for terror' could be read as purpose. The remaining items follow ASV: pārāšîm 'horsemen' is the book's established gloss, although the noun can denote horses (HALOT, recalled); the future 'will bring evil' reads the wayyiqtol with the following weqatal; rāʿ is 'evil' with ASV and JPS 1917, and the 45:7 'calamity' entry is not extended because its rationale rests on the merism with šālôm. At 31:5 psḥ is the verb of Exod 12:13, 23, 27; 'pass over' is the ASV and JPS 1917 rendering, and the Passover echo is kept to commentary. At 31:8 NJPS derives wᵉnās from nss and lāmas from mss ('shrivel', 'pine away'); the line keeps the usual nws 'flee' and mas 'forced labor'. 'Forced labor' is the modern English for the corvée that ASV calls 'taskwork'; the central mas-oved entry keeps 'taskwork' for the compound at Gen 49:15, and that cross-corpus difference is flagged in the editor report. The entry is direct, because every rendering is attested in ASV, JPS 1917 or NJPS, except 31:8 lāmas 'forced labor' and 31:1 'lean on', which give the standard lexical sense (BDB, HALOT) of the noun and verb; no reading is added.

entries.lemma: single-site lexical and textual decisions of Isaiah 33 not covered by a dedicated entry
entries.literal: when you finish(?); the gathering of the locust; like the rushing of locusts, one rushing; firmness of your times; store; their heroes(?); messengers of peace; like the desert; shaking off; will sojourn; burnings of perpetuity; one counting; one weighing; insolent(?); city of our appointed times; untroubled pasture-abode; its cords; your cords; prey of spoil; they plundered plunder
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: 'when thou hast made an end of dealing treacherously'; 'as the caterpillar gathereth: as locusts leap shall men leap upon it'; 'stability in thy times, abundance of salvation'; 'their valiant ones'; 'the ambassadors of peace'; 'like a desert'; 'shake off [their leaves]'; 'dwell … everlasting burnings'; 'he that counted … he that weighed [the tribute]'; 'the fierce people'; 'the city of our solemnities'; 'a quiet habitation'; 'the cords thereof'; 'our lawgiver'; 'Thy tacklings are loosed'; 'the prey of a great spoil'; 'the lame took the prey'. JPS 1917 and NJPS as cited in the chapter commentary (all three checked 2026-11-26).
entries.wohChoice: ASV wording kept except where the book's concordance requires a change. Kept: 33:1 'when you have made an end of dealing treacherously' (klh reading; JPS 1917 'weary' = lʾh in commentary); 33:4 'as the caterpillar gathers; as locusts leap, so they leap upon it' (indefinite 'they' for ASV's supplied 'men'; future tense with ASV); 33:6 'stability in your times, an abundance of salvation'; 33:7 MT ʾerʾellām 'their valiant ones' (NJPS 'the Arielites' and the repointing 'I will appear to them' in commentary); 33:9 'like a desert' (common noun, as 35:1, 6; 40:3) and 'shake off their leaves' (object supplied as in ASV); 33:14 gûr 'dwell' (as 11:6; 'sojourn' at 16:4 and 23:7 for a stay abroad) and 'everlasting burnings'; 33:18 'the one who counted … the one who weighed' (participle, no supplied object); 33:19 'the fierce people'; 33:20 'the city of our appointed feasts' (môʿăḏîm as 1:14) and 'a quiet habitation' (šaʾănān 'quiet' as 32:18; 'peaceful' stays for nᵉwēh šālôm 32:18); 33:22 'our judge … our lawgiver … our king'. Changed: 33:7 malʾăḵê šālôm 'the messengers of peace' (malʾāḵ 'messenger' as 14:32; 18:2; 42:19; 44:26; ASV 'ambassadors'); 33:20 and 33:23 ḥeḇel 'cords' in both verses (ASV 'tacklings' at 33:23); 33:23 baz 'plunder' in the cognate object 'the lame took the plunder' (šālāl 'spoil' / baz 'plunder' as 10:6; ASV 'prey' for both ʿaḏ and baz).
entries.rationale: Isaiah 33 is a liturgy built from short, compressed clauses, and several of its words are rare (kannᵉlōṯᵉḵā, ʾerʾellām, nôʿāz and yiṣʿān are found only here) or uncertain in every version; NJPS marks vv. 4, 6 and 23 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'. The entry keeps ASV's reading wherever it translates MT and departs from it only where ASV's English would hide a distinction the book draws elsewhere. malʾāḵ is rendered 'messenger(s)' at every Isaiah site translated so far (14:32; 18:2, where ṣîrîm is 'envoys'; 30:4 draft; 42:19; 44:26); 37:36 and 63:9 are not bound by this choice. So 'ambassadors' at 33:7 would give one noun two English words without a lexical reason. ḥeḇel is the same noun in 33:20 (the tent's cords) and 33:23 (the ship's rigging), and the passage turns on the contrast between cords that will not snap and cords that hang slack, so the line uses 'cords' twice; 'tacklings' (ASV, JPS 1917) and 'ropes' (NJPS) would separate them. bāzᵉzû baz is a cognate accusative, and the book renders baz 'plunder' beside šālāl 'spoil' at 10:6; ASV's 'took the prey' gives baz the word it also uses for ʿaḏ in the same verse. Every rendering is a standard lexical gloss (BDB; HALOT; recalled); most are the wording of at least one of ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS, and the three concordance changes are argued above, so the claim is direct. Readings not taken (JPS 1917 'weary' at 33:1, NJPS 'the Arielites' at 33:7, NJPS 'throat' at 33:18, NJPS 'barbarian' at 33:19) are reported in commentary with their source.

entries.translit: ʾaddîr (33:21 ʾaddîr YHWH lānû; ṣî ʾaddîr; 10:34 bᵉʾaddîr)
entries.strongs: H117 (ʾaddîr); root ʾdr 'be wide, great, majestic' (H142). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: ʾaddîr 'mighty, majestic, noble'
entries.partOfSpeech: adjective, also used as a noun
entries.literal: great, mighty, majestic
entries.standardEnglish: ASV 'in majesty' and 'gallant [ship]' (33:21), 'a mighty one' (10:34); JPS 1917 'in majesty' and 'gallant ship' (33:21); NJPS 'in His greatness' and 'mighty craft' (33:21) (checked 2026-11-26)
entries.wohChoice: 'mighty' for ʾaddîr in Isaiah: 33:21 'there YHWH will be mighty for us … and no mighty ship shall pass'; 10:34 'by a mighty one' (stable, already so printed). Never 'majesty' or 'majestic', which the book reserves for the root gʾh (gāʾôn, gēʾûṯ); never 'glorious', reserved for kāḇôḏ.
entries.rationale: ʾaddîr is 'great, mighty, majestic' (BDB; HALOT; recalled), said of waters (Exod 15:10), kings (Ps 136:18), nobles (Jer 14:3) and of YHWH (Ps 8:2, 10; 93:4). ASV renders the two occurrences in Isa 33:21 by two different English words, 'majesty' and 'gallant', so an English reader cannot see that the verse sets the might of YHWH against the 'mighty' ships that cannot cross the waters he becomes; NJPS keeps 'mighty' for the second. The wave I-5 rulings reserve 'majesty' for gāʾôn of God (overlays hadar-splendor-isaiah, gaon-pride-human-arrogance-isaiah, geut-majesty-isaiah), so ASV's first rendering is not available here, and the stable 10:34 already prints ʾaddîr 'a mighty one'. 'Mighty' is a standard lexical gloss, used by NJPS in this verse, and carries no interpretive load, so the claim is direct. Cost recorded: 'mighty' also renders gibbôr in the fixed title 'Mighty God' (9:5; 10:21) and in 'mighty men'; the two words never meet in one verse, and the overlap is accepted. 'Mighty One' also renders ʾăḇîr in the title ʾăḇîr yiśrāʾēl / yaʿăqōḇ (1:24 stable; 49:26; 60:16); the roots do not share a verse. Orchestrator: ISA-10:34 is in a stable chapter; its English line is unchanged, and its glossaryRefs need this id when the diff is merged.

entries.translit: yōp̄î (33:17 bᵉyop̄yô 'in his beauty'; 3:24 taḥaṯ yōp̄î 'instead of beauty')
entries.strongs: H3308 (yōp̄î); root yph 'be beautiful' (H3302). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: yōp̄î 'beauty'
entries.literal: beauty, fairness
entries.standardEnglish: 'beauty' (ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS at 33:17, all checked 2026-11-26; ASV 'beauty' at 3:24)
entries.wohChoice: 'beauty' for yōp̄î: 33:17 'the king in his beauty'; 3:24 'branding instead of beauty' (stable, already so printed). The English word is shared with ṣᵉḇî (overlay tsevi-beauty-isaiah); the sharing is recorded here and in that entry. If a later site puts yōp̄î and ṣᵉḇî in one verse, its Editor must separate them ('loveliness' or 'fairness' for yōp̄î is the recorded fallback).
entries.rationale: yōp̄î is the abstract noun of yph 'be beautiful', the ordinary Hebrew word for beauty of person or thing (Ezek 16:14; 28:7; Ps 45:12; BDB, recalled), and 'beauty' is its standard English in every version consulted. The book already uses 'beauty' for ṣᵉḇî 'ornament, splendour' (overlay tsevi-beauty-isaiah) so that 'glory' stays reserved for kāḇôḏ, and that entry does not claim 'beauty' exclusively. A distinct English word for yōp̄î ('loveliness', 'fairness') was considered and rejected: it would be less exact than 'beauty' for the plain word, would break the famous and universal rendering of 33:17, and would also require revising the stable 3:24. The two nouns do not stand in the same verse anywhere in Isaiah, so the shared English hides no contrast the Hebrew draws; the overlap is recorded so that a reader can audit it. The claim is direct because 'beauty' is the lexical gloss.

entries.translit: ʾĕnôš (33:8 lōʾ ḥāšaḇ ʾĕnôš; 13:12 ʾôqîr ʾĕnôš; 24:6 wᵉnišʾar ʾĕnôš mizʿār)
entries.strongs: H582 (ʾĕnôš). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entries.lemma: ʾĕnôš 'human being, mortal; humankind' (poetic generic noun)
entries.literal: a human being, mortal(s)
entries.wohChoice: 'mortal(s)' for ʾĕnôš used as a substantive in Isaiah: 33:8 'he regards no mortal'; 13:12 'I will make a mortal rarer than fine gold' and 24:6 'few mortals are left' (both stable, already so printed). Context clauses (stable lines, not reopened): attributive 'human' in lᵉḇaḇ ʾĕnôš 'every human heart' (13:7); the idiom ḥereṭ ʾĕnôš 'the pen of a man' (8:1), i.e. ordinary script. Expected later sites of the substantive rule (not yet in appliesTo; their Editors apply or record a departure): 51:7, 51:12, 56:2. Not governed by adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah, which covers ʾāḏām and ʾîš.
entries.rationale: ʾĕnôš is a poetic generic noun for the human being, often with a nuance of weakness and mortality (Ps 8:5; 90:3; 103:15; BDB; HALOT; recalled). Wave I-4 rule 13 makes generic human nouns gender-neutral, and the stable chapters already render ʾĕnôš as a substantive by 'mortal' (13:12, beside ʾāḏām 'a human being') and 'mortals' (24:6), the rendering NJPS also uses at 33:8 ('Mortal man'). The Translator's 'he regards no one' was gender-neutral but dropped the noun, so the reader could not see that the oppressor's contempt is for human beings as such; 'no mortal' keeps the noun and the book's existing English. The renderings are standard lexical glosses with no interpretive load, so the claim is direct. Orchestrator: ISA-13:12 and ISA-24:6 are in stable chapters; their English lines are unchanged, and their glossaryRefs need this id when the diff is merged.

entries.strongs: H3917. Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified. Akkadian cognate lilītu: CAD L, s.v. lilītu (recalled, page not checked).
entries.lemma: lîlîṯ, a female night-demon (Akkadian lilītu)
entries.partOfSpeech: noun, feminine singular; hapax legomenon in the Hebrew Bible
entries.literal: a lilith, a female demon of the lilû class (popularly heard as 'the one of the night', from layil 'night')
entries.standardEnglish: the night-monster (ASV; JPS 1917, checked 2026-11-26); the lilith, with note 'A kind of demon' (NJPS, checked 2026-11-26); the screech owl (KJV, checked); Lilith (NRSV, not verified); the night hag (RSV, recalled)
entries.wohChoice: 'the night-monster' at 34:14, a class noun with the article and in lower case, with the feminine verbs kept ('there the night-monster shall settle, and shall find for herself a place of rest'). The capitalised personal name 'Lilith' and the animal reading 'screech owl' are recorded in commentary and not used in the line. NJPS 'the lilith' (lower-case class noun, following the Akkadian–Sumerian philology) is reported as the alternative; the founder kept 'the night-monster' (sign-off 2026-11-26).
entries.rationale: lîlîṯ occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, among the creatures that occupy ruined Edom. It is the Akkadian lilītu, a female demon of the lilû class, beside the masculine lilû and the ardat-lilî (CAD L, recalled); the class name is usually traced to Sumerian líl 'wind, breath', and in Hebrew the word was heard as if it came from layil 'night'. The ASV and JPS 1917 rendering 'the night-monster' reflects the Hebrew hearing of the word as a creature of the night (layil) and is the public-domain baseline; it does not follow the Akkadian–Sumerian philology, in which the class name goes back to líl 'wind, breath', though it does keep the word a class of demon. NJPS 'the lilith', with its note 'A kind of demon', is the alternative that follows the philology: it keeps the class noun in lower case without importing either the 'night' association or the personal name, and it is reported as the alternative; the founder kept 'the night-monster' (sign-off 2026-11-26). The capitalised 'Lilith' (NRSV, not verified) turns the class noun into a personal name and brings in the later figure of the Talmud (long hair, b. ʿErub. 100b; wings, b. Nid. 24b; seizing sleepers, b. Šabb. 151b; recalled) and of the medieval Alphabet of Ben Sira, where Lilith is Adam's first wife (B. Hutter, 'Lilith', DDD, 2nd ed., 1999; recalled); that figure is reception history and is kept to commentary. The KJV 'screech owl' takes lîlîṯ as a bird (KJV renders śāʿîr in the same verse 'the satyr', so it does not take every creature as an animal); the Akkadian evidence does not support a bird for this word, and the reading is recorded in commentary. The entry is direct: 'the night-monster' is the public-domain baseline and agrees with the lexical consensus that lîlîṯ is a demon; the alternative 'the lilith' would also be direct (NJPS). The wave I-5 rulings require the word to be rendered by philology and the lens-salient reading of Lilith to stay out of the line; the line encodes neither the later personal figure nor any project reading, and the one labelled speculative paragraph at 34:14 states that the Raëlian canon texts in data-library neither cite the verse nor name Lilith.

entries.wohChoice: One English name per Hebrew creature name across Isaiah's ruin passages: ṣiyyîm 'desert creatures' and ʾiyyîm 'hyenas' (as at 13:21-22); tannîm 'jackals' (as at 13:22; 35:7; 43:20; distinct from tannîn 'dragon', central taninim); bᵉnôṯ yaʿănāh 'ostriches' (13:21; 43:20); qāʾaṯ 'pelican'; qippōḏ 'porcupine' (as at 14:23); yanšôp̄ 'owl'; qippôz 'dart-snake'; dayyôṯ 'kites'. ʿōrēḇ 'raven' is governed by central yonah-orev, śāʿîr 'wild goat' by lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah, and lîlîṯ by lilit-night-monster-isaiah-34.
entries.rationale: Isaiah describes the ruin of a city by listing the creatures that move into it, at 13:21-22, 14:23 and 34:11-15 (cf. Zeph 2:14; Jer 50:39), and several names recur across these passages. Most of the identifications are uncertain (NJPS notes at 34:11 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain' and at 34:14 that most of the creatures in vv. 14-15 'cannot be identified with certainty'), so no rendering can claim to be the right animal. What the translation can do is give each Hebrew name one English name wherever it recurs, so that the reader of 34:11-15 recognises the creatures of 13:21-22 and 14:23. The stable chapters fix ṣiyyîm 'desert creatures', ʾiyyîm 'hyenas' (NRSV), tannîm 'jackals', bᵉnôṯ yaʿănāh 'ostriches' and qippōḏ 'porcupine', and this entry applies them at 34:11-14. Where the book has no earlier decision, the ASV names are kept (qāʾaṯ 'pelican', yanšôp̄ 'owl', qippôz 'dart-snake', dayyôṯ 'kites'); the alternatives of JPS 1917 and NJPS are given in commentary. qippōḏ is the hardest case: in the bird list of 34:11 a bird is likely (JPS 1917 'bittern', NJPS 'owls'), and Zeph 2:14, where qāʾaṯ and qippōḏ lodge on the capitals of columns, points the same way, but ASV's 'porcupine' is kept for concordance with 14:23; if a later pass changes it, both sites change together. tannîm 'jackals' is a different word from tannîn 'dragon, sea monster' (27:1), and the central taninim entry is not applied. The entry is direct: each rendering is that of ASV or of the stable chapters, which follow ASV or NRSV. The orchestrator may add ISA-13:21, ISA-13:22, ISA-14:23 and ISA-43:20 to appliesTo with no change to those lines, and the chapter-35 Editor may add ISA-35:7 (tannîm 'jackals').

entries.lemma: lexical and syntactic cruxes of Isaiah 34
entries.partOfSpeech: nouns; Niphal and Qal verbs; nominal clause
entries.literal: its fullness … its offspring; they shall melt; they shall rot … it shall wither as the withering of … and as a withering (one); a sword belongs to YHWH; its nobles … they shall call; enclosure
entries.standardEnglish: 34:1 ASV and JPS 1917 'the fulness thereof … all things that come forth (of/from) it'; NJPS 'those in it … what it brings forth'. 34:3 ASV and JPS 1917 'the mountains shall be melted with their blood'; NJPS 'the hills shall be drenched with their blood'. 34:4 ASV 'shall be dissolved … fade away … as a fading [leaf]'; JPS 1917 'moulder away … fall down … a falling fig'; NJPS 'molder … wither … shriveled fruit'. 34:6 ASV and JPS 1917 'The sword of Jehovah/the LORD is filled with blood'; NJPS 'The LORD has a sword; it is sated with blood'. 34:12 ASV 'They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there'; JPS 1917 'As for her nobles, none shall be there to be called to the kingdom'; NJPS 'It shall be called, "No kingdom is there"' (note: meaning uncertain). 34:13 ASV 'a court'; JPS 1917 'an enclosure'; NJPS 'an abode'. All checked 2026-11-26.
entries.wohChoice: 34:1 ûmᵉlōʾāh 'and its fullness', ṣeʾĕṣāʾeyhā 'all that comes forth from it' (ASV). 34:3 nāmassû 'shall be melted' (ASV, JPS 1917). 34:4 nāmaqqû 'shall rot away' (line change from the draft's ASV 'shall be dissolved'); nbl 'fade' throughout the verse ('shall fade away, as the leaf fades from the vine, and as a fading leaf from the fig tree'), with 'leaf' supplied as in ASV. 34:6 ḥereḇ laYHWH 'The sword of YHWH' (ASV, JPS 1917). 34:12 ASV kept: 'Its nobles they shall call to the kingdom, but none shall be there'. 34:13 ḥāṣîr 'a court' (ASV).
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator asked whether to keep the ASV or follow a modern version, and the entry records the decision so that the English line is backed by the glossary. The one line change is at 34:4. The verb mqq means 'rot, fester, waste away' (BDB; HALOT; recalled): wounds fester (Ps 38:6), flesh rots (Zech 14:12), and the noun maq is 'rottenness' at Isa 3:24 and 5:24 in this translation. ASV's 'shall be dissolved' gives the result without the image, while JPS 1917 'moulder away' and NJPS 'molder' keep the decay; 'shall rot away' keeps the root's sense and its English family in the book. In the same verse nbl is 'fade', as ASV has it and as the book has it at 40:7-8 ('the flower fades'); the participle nōḇeleṯ has no noun, and 'leaf' is supplied with ASV rather than JPS 1917 'fig' or NJPS 'fruit'. The other items keep ASV: at 34:3 the literal 'melted' over NJPS's paraphrase 'drenched'; at 34:6 the genitive construal 'The sword of YHWH' (ASV, JPS 1917) over NJPS's possessive nominal clause, a difference of syntax and not of sense; at 34:12, a crux (NJPS 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'), the ASV construal, which needs no emendation, with the readings of JPS 1917 and NJPS and the proposal that a word has fallen out given in commentary; at 34:13 ḥāṣîr is the 'enclosure, abode' noun related to ḥāṣēr 'court' and not ḥāṣîr 'grass', and ASV's 'a court' gives that sense. At 34:1 mᵉlōʾāh 'its fullness' (ASV, JPS 1917) keeps the noun, where NJPS paraphrases 'those in it'. None of the choices carries a lens.

entries.wohChoice: 35:1 yᵉśuśûm 'shall be glad' (final -m not rendered as a suffix; consonants unchanged); midbār 'wilderness', ṣiyyāh 'the dry land', ʿărāḇāh 'desert' (common noun, as 35:6; 40:3; cf. 33:9; at 43:19-20 the pair is midbār / yᵉšîmôn); ḥăḇaṣṣeleṯ 'the rose' (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS text; crocus/asphodel identification in commentary). 35:2 'rejoice even with joy and singing' (ASV); hakkarmel 'Carmel', the place name, beside Lebanon and Sharon (against 'the fruitful field' of 10:18; 29:17; 32:15-16, where the context is agricultural); rnn 'sing/singing' through the chapter (35:2, 6, 10). 35:3 'make firm the feeble knees' (JPS 1917 verb, ASV adjective). 35:4 'those who are of a fearful heart'; ASV/JPS 1917 construal 'your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God' kept, NJPS exclamation 'Behold your God!' (cf. 40:9) in commentary; 'Be strong, do not fear!' (central al-tira formula entry not applied). 35:6 'the lame … like a deer … the mute' (generic singular without supplied 'man', wave I-4 ruling 13; current English for 'hart', 'dumb'). 35:7 šārāḇ 'the glowing sand' (ASV); tannîm 'jackals' (as 13:22; 43:20; 34:13; KJV 'dragons' = confusion with tannîn); riḇṣāh 'where they lay' (ASV); ḥāṣîr lᵉqāneh wāḡōmeʾ 'grass shall become reeds and rushes' (MT vowels, ḥāṣîr 'grass' with ASV; lᵉ of becoming as in the verse's first two clauses, replacing ASV's 'with'); the JPS 1917/NJPS 'enclosure/abode' reading (cf. 34:13) in commentary. 35:8 maslûl wāḏereḵ 'a highway … and a way' (MT; dittography deletion and NJPS in commentary); dereḵ haqqōḏeš 'the Way of Holiness', capitalised as a called name (cf. 19:18 'the City of Destruction'); wᵉhûʾ-lāmô 'but it shall be for them' (no supplied words; ASV '[the redeemed]', emendation 'for His people' in commentary); hōlēḵ dereḵ waʾĕwîlîm lōʾ yiṯʿû 'the wayfarers, even fools, shall not go astray' (athnach construal; no gendered noun, no supplied 'therein'). 35:9 lōʾ timmāṣēʾ 'they shall not be found there' (ASV plural for the 3fs collective); 'the redeemed shall walk there' (ASV supplied adverb kept). 35:10 pᵉḏûyê YHWH 'the ransomed of YHWH' (central goel-geullah context clause, founder sign-off 2026-11-26); śāśôn wᵉśimḥāh 'gladness and joy' (ASV; śûś/śāśôn = glad/gladness, śimḥāh = joy inside the chapter; stable 22:13 has the reverse order of English nouns, recorded, not changed).
entries.rationale: Each item is a site where the line keeps the Masoretic text and chooses among the renderings of the standard versions; none carries a project reading. (1) The final -m of yᵉśuśûm is not an object suffix in ASV, JPS 1917 or NJPS (KJV 'glad for them' is the exception), and it is usually explained as a dittography of the following m or as an enclitic mem; rendering no suffix changes no consonant. (2) ḥăḇaṣṣeleṯ is a flower of uncertain identity (Song 2:1); 'rose' is the English of ASV, JPS 1917 and the NJPS text, and NJPS itself notes 'Lit. "crocus"', so the line keeps the familiar word and the commentary gives the botany. (3) hakkarmel is 'the fruitful field' in the stable chapters, where it stands beside forest and wilderness; at 35:2 it stands between Lebanon and Sharon, both regions, and every version checked prints 'Carmel'; the article is normal with the mountain (1 Kgs 18:19-20; Amos 1:2), and the same three regions wither at 33:9. (4) At 35:4 the accents allow both the ASV/JPS 1917 construal and the NJPS exclamation; the line keeps the public-domain construal, which needs no change of word order. (5) At 35:7 the noun ḥāṣîr is kept as 'grass' with ASV, but the preposition lᵉ is given the sense 'become' that it has twice earlier in the same verse (laʾăḡam, lᵉmabbûʿê mayim), so the line reads 'grass shall become reeds and rushes', the wording of RSV, ESV and NRSVue (checked by the Reviewer on BibleGateway, 2026-11-26); ASV's 'with' is not the sense lᵉ has elsewhere in this verse. The alternative, ḥāṣîr 'court, abode' as at 34:13 (JPS 1917, NJPS), is recorded in commentary. tannîm 'jackals' matches the stable 13:22 and 43:20. (6) At 35:8 the line follows MT 'a highway … and a way', capitalises the called name 'the Way of Holiness' as 19:18 capitalises 'the City of Destruction', and renders wᵉhûʾ-lāmô 'but it shall be for them' without ASV's supplied '[the redeemed]', which interprets an unclear antecedent; NJPS also prints 'for them'. The athnach on lāmô puts hōlēḵ dereḵ in the last clause, as in ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS. (7) Modern English replaces ASV's 'confirm' (35:3), 'hart' and 'dumb' (35:6), and the supplied 'man' and 'wayfaring men' are dropped under wave I-4 ruling 13 for generic human nouns. (8) The joy vocabulary follows ASV inside the chapter; the inconsistency with stable 22:13 is recorded and not changed, because no entry fixes the book's joy vocabulary. XXVIII, not DJD 32; lexica, grammars and NRSV not verified.
